sentences.text: This video can not be played Moment 'hitman' mimed shooting police during arrest A teenager who travelled from Norway to the UK to carry out a "hit" for an organised crime group has been sentenced to 20 years' detention.
sentences.article_title: Norwegian teen 'hitman' detained for UK murder plot

sentences.text: Johannes Natland, 19, was arrested in a hotel room in Huddersfield, West Yorkshire, with two working guns and 19 rounds of live ammunition in March 2025, the Old Bailey previously heard.
sentences.article_title: Norwegian teen 'hitman' detained for UK murder plot

sentences.text: During his retrial, a jury heard the teen was "recruited" by the Foxtrot Network, which was described as a Swedish organised crime group backed by the Iranian regime.
sentences.article_title: Norwegian teen 'hitman' detained for UK murder plot

sentences.text: Natland, who had admitted to possession of the firearms and ammunition, was unanimously found guilty of conspiracy to murder and sentenced at Woolwich Crown Court on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Norwegian teen 'hitman' detained for UK murder plot

sentences.text: The Foxtrot Network has been sanctioned by both the UK and the US for its close links to the Iranian government, with Natland's target remaining unclear.
sentences.article_title: Norwegian teen 'hitman' detained for UK murder plot

sentences.text: Commander Helen Flanagan, head of Counter Terrorism Policing London, said: "We haven't been able to establish exactly who the intended victim was." The Foxtrot Network is known for pioneering a relatively new phenomenon of hiring teenage killers that Europol has called "violence-as-a-service" (VaaS).
sentences.article_title: Norwegian teen 'hitman' detained for UK murder plot

sentences.text: At the sentencing hearing, Mrs Justice Cheema-Grubb told Natland: "The Foxtrot Network is an organised crime group which has developed an arm's-length method of recruiting young people to carry out violent crimes.
sentences.article_title: Norwegian teen 'hitman' detained for UK murder plot

sentences.text: "You were recruited to travel to England to kill an unidentified target." Natland had been offered 270,000 Norwegian Kroner, about £21,000, to carry out the killing.
sentences.article_title: Norwegian teen 'hitman' detained for UK murder plot

sentences.text: He flew into Manchester Airport on an emergency passport on 17 March 2025, shortly after his 18th birthday.
sentences.article_title: Norwegian teen 'hitman' detained for UK murder plot

sentences.text: Natland was guided by videos on the messaging app Signal to Huddersfield, where the guns, a stolen car and a stash of cash were hidden.
sentences.article_title: Norwegian teen 'hitman' detained for UK murder plot

sentences.text: He was prevented from carrying out the hit after Norwegian police arrested the teenager who had recruited him for the Foxtrot Network and found messages about the UK plot on his phone.
sentences.article_title: Norwegian teen 'hitman' detained for UK murder plot

sentences.text: There was then a race against time to find Natland before he located his unknown target in England.
sentences.article_title: Norwegian teen 'hitman' detained for UK murder plot

sentences.text: Addressing Natland, the judge said: "At the heart of this case is a stark fact.
sentences.article_title: Norwegian teen 'hitman' detained for UK murder plot

sentences.text: You agreed to assassinate another human being, a stranger to you, in a foreign country.
sentences.article_title: Norwegian teen 'hitman' detained for UK murder plot

sentences.text: "You knew nothing of that person's life or circumstances.
sentences.article_title: Norwegian teen 'hitman' detained for UK murder plot

sentences.text: When he saw officers at the door, he mimed shooting one of them with his hands before he was pushed against the wall and handcuffed.
sentences.article_title: Norwegian teen 'hitman' detained for UK murder plot

sentences.text: "There was pressure because he'd come into the country, and we knew his intention was to carry out a murder on UK soil," said Flanagan.
sentences.article_title: Norwegian teen 'hitman' detained for UK murder plot

sentences.text: "We had to move at pace and we intervened really quickly, and just before he sort of moved towards committing that murder." Natland grew up in the oil city of Stavanger in south-west Norway.
sentences.article_title: Norwegian teen 'hitman' detained for UK murder plot

sentences.text: Despite being a promising young footballer, he started taking drugs aged 13 and later dropped out of school.
sentences.article_title: Norwegian teen 'hitman' detained for UK murder plot

sentences.text: He previously told the Old Bailey that by last year he was taking drugs "pretty much every day".

sentences.text: The defendant said he spent a short period in a "home for problem children" where he met one of those who later recruited him to the Foxtrot Network, a teenager with the username UnknownHustler.

sentences.text: Mrs Justice Cheema-Grubb told Natland: "You agreed to be the enforcer and pursued it, despite numerous opportunities to extricate yourself." Within two days of being recruited, Natland flew from Stavanger to Manchester, using the emergency passport as his normal one had expired.

sentences.text: He was stopped by Border Force officials in Manchester and was told to return to the airport to catch the next direct flight home.

sentences.text: "I can kill someone and life will be wonderful." Giving evidence, Natland said he wanted to look "cool" to his peers but it was just "bravado" and inside he was "terrified".

sentences.text: He told jurors: "I wasn't an international assassin.

sentences.text: "The intended target of this specific assassination has never been identified, and we found no evidence of any direct link to Iran in this case.

sentences.text: Five children were found alive under the body of Nansi Williams following the disaster On 21 October 1966, as a primary school and surrounding homes in Aberfan were engulfed by slurry from a collapsed coal tip, a dinner lady was collecting money from pupils.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: Within moments, 144 people were dead, including 116 children, on what was the last day of class at Pantglas Junior School before the half-term holiday.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: But five children were saved that day by the heroic actions of Nansi Williams, who died shielding the group.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "Apparently she was holding as much of us as she could, and trying to get us under a table," said Aberfan survivor Paul Harries, who has spoken to the media for the first time.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: Harries, who was aged six at the time, was one of the five who was found alive under Williams' body.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "She gave everything to give us a future, and she lost everything, he said.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "Nansi Williams was a hero.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: My hero." He continued: "If it hadn't been for Nansi Williams, then instead of 116 children dying that morning it would have been 121.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "It would have been us, 100%." As the 60th anniversary of the disaster approaches, Williams will be honoured with a purple plaque , external to commemorate her courage.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: Paul Harries was giving his dinner money to Nansi Williams when the school was engulfed The King, Queen and Prince of Wales will visit Aberfan, in Merthyr Tydfil county, next week to mark the anniversary, following on from the late Queen Elizabeth who visited Aberfan eight times .
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "The only reason I'm speaking about it now is because Nansi's story needs to be told and recognised for what she has done," Paul, now 66, said.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: He recalled how an avalanche of slurry swept through the school just minutes after lessons began.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: He had walked from the infant school to the junior school hall to pay a shilling for his school dinner.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: It was there Williams was collecting the money from him and four other children.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: When a colliery waste tip collapsed, slurry crashed into Pantglas Junior School, killing 116 children and 28 adults "The infant school was totally missed by the tips," he added.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "So it was only by chance that we were not in the infant school, which was safe.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: We were in the junior school which caught the brunt of it." Harries cannot remember the moment the building collapsed, but said: "I can remember being dug out.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "I was rushed straight to hospital with the other four children that were buried with me." It was only later that he learnt of Nansi's heroics.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "My mother and father told me the story," he said.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "They said 'your dinner lady died protecting you five children'." When rescuers found them, Williams was still shielding the group.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: Nansi Williams grew up in Aberfan and worked as a dinner lady and playground supervisor at Pantglas Junior School Williams, who was 44, was a familiar figure to that generation of Aberfan children.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: Another pupil, Janett Bickley, remembers her as a kind and popular presence.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "Oh, Nansi was lovely," she said.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "My mother and Nansi were friends.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "If you were lucky you could hold her hand in the yard at break time." She recalled proudly walking around the playground thinking "I'm holding Nansi's hand today".
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: Like many pupils, Bickley remembered Williams collecting dinner money and leading children to lunch.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: Janett Bickley recalled how all the children were very fond of Nansi Williams "She was trying to protect children," she said.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "She died, and they lived." Bickley believes there are many people who should be recognised for their courage on that day, but agreed Williams was a hero.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "I think Nansi went way, way beyond what she needed to do," she said.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "She could have saved her own life.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: She cared more for the children." Nansi's godson, Dai Powell, campaigned for greater recognition and said stories of what happened were passed down through his family for decades.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: No-one will ever touch her," he said.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "We'd all like to think we'd do the same thing, but until it happens we don't really know.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "Her heroism is just unbelievable." Dai Powell has led the campaign for Nansi's courage to be honoured with a purple plaque The purple plaque scheme , external celebrates women who have made important contributions to their communities in Wales or shown exceptional courage.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "She didn't think of herself at all, she just thought of the children," said Rhian Connick, secretary of the Purple Plaque Committee.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: The plaque will be placed near the cemetery in Aberfan For Harries, the plaque will ensure her story survives long after those who remember her are gone.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "Every year I go straight to Nansi's grave and put flowers there," he said.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "My family know the story of Nansi because if it hadn't been for her, they wouldn't be here today.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "There would be no son, no grandchildren.
sentences.article_title: The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

sentences.text: "It's something permanent now.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Same-day test helps detect hidden infections in critically ill children A pioneering same-day test has been used to detect hidden and drug-resistant infections among children in intensive care.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Respiratory samples from more than 100 critically ill young patients at London's Great Ormond Street Hospital (GOSH) were sent for what is known as metagenomic testing. , external It can identify bacteria, viruses and fungi from a single sample, which in many cases influences what doctors prescribe.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Metagenomics can detect infections that standard tests miss, meaning better outcomes for some critically ill patients.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: In March, 10-year-old Willow Crowther became dangerously ill with pneumonia, which triggered a seizure and multiple cardiac arrests.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Willow, from Kent, was admitted to intensive care at GOSH.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Her mum, Stacey Moore, was told she had a 50% chance of survival.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: "The consultant said... we should bring our family up to say goodbye to her.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: This is how critical and in how much danger she was of passing away." The team at GOSH used metagenomics - a diagnostic test that works by sequencing all genetic material present, in contrast to conventional methods where clinicians need to decide in advance what they're looking for.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: The test identified that Willow had a drug-resistant bacterial infection which needed a different antibiotic to the one she had been prescribed.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: The test helped doctors identify which antibiotic would be effective in treating Willow "The fact that they had a test there available to her was paramount.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: It saved her life," said Stacey.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: "It's a miracle she's here and we're extremely grateful for that," added Willow's dad, Russ.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: With the right treatment, Willow was eventually able to recover from her infection, but needed several months in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: She is one of many patients at the children's hospital to benefit from the new type of testing.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: During a study in 2024-5 metagenomic testing was used on 122 critically ill children in the paediatric intensive care unit (ICU) at GOSH.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: The results have now been published in the Lancet Microbe.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Metagenomic testing analyses all genetic material in a sample and can detect thousands of different pathogens.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: By contrast, the most common method of identifying bacteria is by trying to culture them in Petri dishes, a technology that has been used since Victorian times.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Another test, PCR, can identify viruses and some bacteria, but doctors need to specify what they are trying to detect.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Metagenomics testing at GOSH was able to identify around nine in 10 bacteria and viruses and all fungi in samples.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Willow celebrated her 10th birthday in August In a quarter of cases, the results influenced prescribing decisions, including starting, stopping or changing an antibiotic.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Dr Sam Ray, consultant in paediatric intensive care medicine at GOSH and co-author of the study said traditional testing required clinicians to make an educated guess about which infection they were looking for.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: "The study has helped us to spot infections we would have missed, get children on the right treatment and stop antibiotics when we know they aren't going to work.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: "Removing unnecessary treatment is incredibly important for the fight against growing antimicrobial resistance." Metagenomic testing at GOSH also detected 50 organisms not identified by routine diagnostics, meaning it could play an early warning role against new infections.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Dr Julianne Brown, head of the GOSH Metagenomics Service and co-senior author of the study said the new testing was being gradually rolled out to around 30 intensive care units across the UK treating both adults and children.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: "It could be a powerful tool for identifying new infections that pose a pandemic threat," she added.

sentences.text: Irene Breen told the BBC her business suffered a significant financial hit from the restrictions When Irene Breen got a notification in January 2025 that Instagram was removing adverts for her company's pregnancy pillows, she was confused.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: What was so offensive about a pillow?
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: She was later told on a call with Meta that the problem was the word "pregnancy".
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: "We had to scrub the word from our entire website… from the product name," Breen said.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: "We had to remove all our URLs which had pregnancy in them and rename them all." The restrictions were eventually lifted but, she said, it took 10 months of conversations with Instagram's parent company Meta - by which time her business had suffered a significant financial hit.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: Meta, which also owns Facebook, declined to comment on specific cases, but told the BBC that while businesses can run adverts that promote wellness, sexual health and reproductive products and services, there are restrictions to avoid users across countries and cultures having a negative experience.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: It's not just businesses taking out paid adverts who claim their content has been unfairly restricted.

sentences.text: Women's health creators and charities have told us their content has been removed, had sensitivity filters added, or had its reach suppressed - a practice known as "shadowbanning".

sentences.text: Dr Stephen Brearey said he began to associate Letby with unexplained deaths in 2015 A senior doctor who raised suspicions about Lucy Letby has said he should have gone to police sooner.
sentences.article_title: Doctor regrets not going to police earlier about Lucy Letby

sentences.text: Dr Stephen Brearey was the lead neonatal consultant at the Countess of Chester Hospital when the nurse murdered seven babies and attempted to murder seven others.
sentences.article_title: Doctor regrets not going to police earlier about Lucy Letby

sentences.text: In his first interview since the publication of the Thirlwall Inquiry report into what happened, Brearey reflected on the effect on staff and said he had "naively" assumed senior managers would respond to suspicions about the nurse's involvement in a series of baby deaths.
sentences.article_title: Doctor regrets not going to police earlier about Lucy Letby

sentences.text: The inquiry found a "toxic negativity" within the NHS that continued to discourage staff from speaking out, despite stronger whistleblowing guidance, and said regulation was lacking.
sentences.article_title: Doctor regrets not going to police earlier about Lucy Letby

sentences.text: Brearey claimed his warnings about Letby were repeatedly ignored by bosses at the hospital, which is now under new management - and also fears cultural change at the NHS will take time to implement.
sentences.article_title: Doctor regrets not going to police earlier about Lucy Letby

sentences.text: "I was naively thinking that raising concerns with senior managers, they had the same values that I did and, once they got it, they would be thinking the same way," he said.
sentences.article_title: Doctor regrets not going to police earlier about Lucy Letby

sentences.text: The doctor led a group of seven consultants who shared the same concerns about Letby.
sentences.article_title: Doctor regrets not going to police earlier about Lucy Letby

sentences.text: Hospital bosses carried out a series of internal reviews into increased infant mortality in 2015 and 2016, but Cheshire Police was not asked to investigate until May 2017.
sentences.article_title: Doctor regrets not going to police earlier about Lucy Letby

sentences.text: Letby remained employed at the hospital until her arrest more than a year later.
sentences.article_title: Doctor regrets not going to police earlier about Lucy Letby

sentences.text: "I think one of the reasons we got through this and ended up picking up a police investigation is that the seven of us stuck together," he said, speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today programme .
sentences.article_title: Doctor regrets not going to police earlier about Lucy Letby

sentences.text: "It really was the team looking after the team, and colleagues looking after colleagues," he said.
sentences.article_title: Doctor regrets not going to police earlier about Lucy Letby

sentences.text: "It's a bit akin to a soldier in a battle with PTSD being taken out of the battle zone to recover, and yet the staff on the neonatal unit were still coming back to work and being re-traumatised.
sentences.article_title: Doctor regrets not going to police earlier about Lucy Letby

sentences.text: Asked whether the measures would have prevented Letby from carrying out her crimes, Brearey said: "It certainly would have either prevented or hastened an alarm to say things need to be looked at in more detail.
sentences.article_title: Doctor regrets not going to police earlier about Lucy Letby

sentences.text: He said Lady Thirwall had recommended "the uncontroversial duty of every manager to put patients first".
sentences.article_title: Doctor regrets not going to police earlier about Lucy Letby

sentences.text: "It feels a bit of a sad indictment on the organisation when that has to be written down into the contracts of senior managers," he said.
sentences.article_title: Doctor regrets not going to police earlier about Lucy Letby

sentences.text: "It's one thing writing into a contract is another thing actually enacting it into the entire organisation and that takes a cultural change and cultural changes take time, and I very much hope that the NHS and the Department of Health can make that turnaround effectively.
sentences.article_title: Doctor regrets not going to police earlier about Lucy Letby

sentences.text: "Given that there are a number of investigations under way, and that the work of the Criminal Cases Review Commission has not yet completed, it would be inappropriate for us to offer any further comment at this time.
sentences.article_title: Doctor regrets not going to police earlier about Lucy Letby

sentences.text: "Our thoughts remain with the families affected by the tragic events that took place at the Countess of Chester Hospital." In a statement given after the conclusion of the inquiry, the hospital trust said: "We know that no apology or action can undo what happened at our hospital.
sentences.article_title: Doctor regrets not going to police earlier about Lucy Letby

sentences.text: "We are however truly sorry for the events that occurred in 2015 and 2016.
sentences.article_title: Doctor regrets not going to police earlier about Lucy Letby

sentences.text: We acknowledge the findings of the Thirlwall report and will approach its recommendations with openness and a firm commitment to build on the progress we have already made in improving our hospital's governance, safety and culture since that time.
sentences.article_title: Doctor regrets not going to police earlier about Lucy Letby

sentences.text: "We are a different organisation today with new leadership, stronger governance and safety processes, and a more open culture where speaking up is encouraged and acted upon." Letby, from Hereford, who maintains her innocence, has twice been denied permission in 2024 to appeal against her convictions.

sentences.text: Chancellor John Healey is planning to increase taxes on the bank sector, senior banking executives have told the BBC.

sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: The Scottish athlete, who was diagnosed with three inoperable brain tumours two years ago, met Prime Minister Andy Burnham after making an emotional plea on BBC Breakfast for more investment to be put into brain cancer research.
sentences.article_title: Emotional TV plea for cancer research leads to meeting with PM

sentences.text: After the meeting, Burnham announced a new national brain cancer clinical lead and promised a review of brain cancer progress and action to get patients treatment sooner.
sentences.article_title: Emotional TV plea for cancer research leads to meeting with PM

sentences.text: Goodburn, 25, thanked the prime minister and said all three of his requests have been "promised to some extent" but "fleshing out" needs to be done on the details.
sentences.article_title: Emotional TV plea for cancer research leads to meeting with PM

sentences.text: The prime minister described the swimmer an "inspiration to us all" and said he was "delighted" to welcome him to Downing Street.

sentences.text: This video can not be played 'It feels like you're days away from death' - Beth Dobbin Beth Dobbin is so determined to raise awareness of the illness that has decimated her life that she is speaking out, despite knowing it could trigger a brutal deterioration in her health.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: Five years ago, she ran for Great Britain at the Tokyo Olympics.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: Now, at 32, she spends more than 22 hours a day in bed.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: "I've done little things like attend a blood test at the doctors and been in bed for months after.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: So doing this interview, chatting away for 30 minutes, that could have an impact on me in 2027," she says.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: "But I felt like it was really important to do that to get the message out." She now only gets out of bed to eat and use the bathroom.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: Dobbin has been diagnosed with ME, or myalgic encephalomyelitis - a chronic, fluctuating disease, causing symptoms such as sleep problems, problems with thinking and memory, pain and severe, persistent fatigue that does not improve with rest, and more.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: A conversation, or even something so simple as a light too bright or a sound too loud, can cause a "crash" that lasts 24, 48 hours, or in the worst cases, months on end.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: This year, Dobbin has left the house on just five occasions.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: "It's life-decimating like I can't even put into words," she says.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: "I feel like I've lost everything.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: "I have still got my family, but I've lost my independence, my health, the ability to work, the ability to exercise." For Dobbin it all started with back-to-back Covid and glandular fever infections in the winter of 2021-22.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: She had not been unwell with either, only discovering she had contracted both through retrospective tests.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: She had been sleeping a bit more and her running times were slightly down, but nothing that raised alarm.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: As time went on, she noticed soreness in the glands of her neck and armpits and a general sense of not quite feeling herself.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: British Athletics doctors ran tests that gave no answers, so she carried on, assuming it was lingering glandular fever that would eventually pass.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: She qualified for that year's World Championships, Commonwealth Games and European Championships in what was an unusually condensed season owing to the backlog from the pandemic.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: Her health progressively deteriorated.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: At the Worlds, she struggled with a painful throat and was waking at unusual times in the night.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: At the Commonwealths, she was dizzy while running and her body was more sore than normal.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: At the Europeans, she false-started after losing all feeling in her legs while in the blocks.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: She spoke of her "year of hell" in an emotional interview with BBC Sport after that race.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: This video can not be played 'It's been a year from hell' - Dobbin emotional after false start "When the Europeans had finished, I had this huge rest and the symptoms were just piling on.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: Things were getting worse and worse," Dobbin says.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: "I was struggling to stand up, I was sleeping loads, in bed all the time.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: "After six weeks, I went back to training.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: "[Doctors] were just really shocked that I still wasn't doing well and I'd had these viruses months ago.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: "I think I saw four or five different specialists because the symptoms that I was having, they were across multiple [body] systems.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: The condition is also known as chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS), a label Dobbin strongly rejects.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: As a former athlete who balanced working eight-hour shifts with training before turning professional, she says she has "known fatigue my whole life" and believes the term fails to capture the severity of the illness.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: "I wish it was just fatigue, that would be a walk in the park," she says.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: "It's so much more than that.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: If I thought of fatigue in my top 20 symptoms it might just make the cut." Instead, she says, it feels like her entire body "is shutting down; it feels like you are a few days from death".
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: More than 400,000 people in the UK are thought to have ME, although the true figure could exceed one million, with severity ranging from people able to work or study to those requiring round-the-clock care and tube feeding.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: Despite the length of time she spends in bed, Dobbin often feels too unwell to sleep and requires medication to help her do so.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: "Even things like sitting up for a prolonged period of time can take it out of me so I prefer to be just propped up in bed, and that doesn't mean I feel fine.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: It doesn't get rid of my symptoms, but it makes them less hellish." This video can not be played The Olympic sprinter who can't leave her bed For Dobbin's parents and sister Faye, who sit close by to her in support during the interview at the family home in Doncaster, the impact is clear.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: "I'm just so desperate to help her but I can't because there is nothing.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: I'd take her anywhere, I'd take her to America if I had to, but there's nothing," says her father Jim, a former footballer who played for Barnsley, Grimsby and Doncaster Rovers.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: Mum Jean adds: "You wake up every day and just feel sad.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: She should be building her life, living her best life.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: "Every day you worry about how she's going to be that day.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: It's a worry about what our future life's going to be like, who's going look after her if we can't look after her.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: "There is nothing out there.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: You go to the GP and there's nowhere for them to send you to.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: It's really at the back of the queue as far as research, knowledge, expertise, funding." There is no specialist service for ME within the NHS and Dobbin says she has found herself educating GPs about the condition.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: She had to wait 22 months before she got a face-to-face appointment with a private specialist she sourced herself after her British Athletics funding ended.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: On Sunday, Dobbin's younger sister Faye will run the Yorkshire Marathon to raise money for ME Research UK.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: "You just feel so helpless and we've been saying this for years now, what can we do?" Faye says.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: "It feels like [the marathon] is all I can do other than supporting her emotionally.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: "It does feel quite like grief in a way.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: I'm always worried about Beth.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: I'm worried about what kind of day she is having.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: What if she never improves?
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: What if she gets another virus?" Beth Dobbin competes for Scotland at the 2022 Commonwealth Games during a summer in which she was suffering debilitating early symptoms of ME Asked about her future, Dobbin is straight to the point: "It's very bleak, unfortunately.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: She added: "There will be something, I hope, in the future.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: "I said I wanted to speak about it.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: It's not necessarily that I want to discuss it [but] it's raising that awareness.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: And unfortunately, athletes are believed a lot more than the average person.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: "A lot of people that have this illness that I've spoken to have said to me 'I don't get believed, people think I'm lazy'.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: I've never experienced one person that doesn't believe me and that's because, why would an athlete just suddenly stop after 20 years?
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: "I've got a slight platform.
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: If this happened to most people they wouldn't be able to speak about it, so I do feel like I've got a bit of a duty to do that."
sentences.article_title: The Olympic sprinter now bedbound for 22 hours a day

sentences.text: Wales has an education crisis.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: As you dip into the valley on the way into Merthyr Tydfil, a new earthy-toned building dominates the view.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: It's the new site of Saint Carlo Acutis Catholic School.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: With its rooftop science garden, solar panels and floor-to-ceiling windows, it's an impressive sight.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Excited staff and 940 pupils moved into the £50m complex at the start of September.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: But they did so just as the Welsh education system was being painted in a less positive light, with Wales once again ranking the worst of UK nations in global tests.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: "It casts doubt over a system we're proud of and children that we're proud of," says Sarah Hopkins, who's been a headteacher here for eight years.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: She says it doesn't tell the full story but admits "it is disappointing".
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Welsh parents are currently thinking about the next steps for their children, with application deadlines for secondary school places at the end of this month.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: That comes at a time when the test results pose difficult questions about why Wales has so clearly underperformed relative to its closest neighbours.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: And with Wales's devolved government now run by a party other than Labour for the first time ever, can the new Plaid Cymru administration do what it's promised and improve standards?
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Sarah Hopkins started teaching in 1998 - a year before the Welsh Assembly, now the Senedd, took over responsibility for education in Wales from Westminster.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: In that time she's had to navigate many system-wide and school changes.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: The latest challenge has been managing the big move from the old mishmash of 1960s-built classrooms to the vast new building.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: But buildings alone do not drive excellence, and the gap between Wales and the other UK countries is getting wider.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Sarah Hopkins describes the Wales Pisa results as "disappointing" Pisa (Programme for International Student Assessment) measures teenagers' skills in reading, maths and science.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Sat by a sample of 15-year-olds – 3,406 in Wales in 2025, including some in Sarah Hopkins' school - it provides a snapshot of how education systems are performing.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: On the day results were published, Wales' education Minister, Anna Brychan, euphemistically said they were "not where we want them to be".
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Others called them catastrophic.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Wales first took part in the tests in 2006.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: There have been upticks along the way.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: But when the pandemic affected scores across the board in 2022, Wales fell back furthest.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: And the gulf grew in the latest results.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: The OECD, the global economic development body which runs Pisa, says that 20 points equates to roughly a year of learning.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: That would mean Welsh 15-year-olds are about two years behind England's in reading, science and maths.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: In reading, they also trail teenagers in Scotland and Northern Ireland by a year.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: The tests alone don't capture everything schools do to support pupils, "whether that's a clean jumper, whether that's having a pen and a pencil" says Hopkins.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: And there are long-standing debates about the methodology of the tests.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: But nobody in Wales is pretending there's nothing to worry about.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Secondary school league tables and standardised tests at seven, 11 and 14 (SATs) were scrapped.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: A new learning-through-play approach for the youngest pupils was an early flagship policy.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Poor Pisa results in 2010 brought about a drastic reappraisal.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Plain speaking Education Minister Leighton Andrews called the results a "wake-up call" for a "complacent" system and introduced a new raft of reforms.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Alongside a literacy and numeracy drive, Andrews re-introduced accountability measures with annual reading and maths tests for seven-to-14 year olds, and a new school performance regime, called banding.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: The two seemed to relish their occasional public spats over policy.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: But policies introduced by Andrews lost their bite over time.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: The school banding system was changed and eventually dropped altogether during the pandemic.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Tests later evolved into personalised assessments.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: And the focus moved to developing a new curriculum in Wales, something which Andrews recently said was a "distraction" from efforts to drive up standards.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Sir Nick Gibb, a former schools minister at Westminster who worked under Michael Gove, believes the main reason for Wales' Pisa woes is weak accountability.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: He says "schools are spending billions of pounds of public money and they're not being held to account for the results that they produce".
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: He argues that focusing on the "science of learning" paid dividends with England's move up international education rankings.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Primary schools in England were told they had to use a structured form of phonics to teach young children to read.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: This was reinforced with a phonics screening check for six-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Sir Nick claims education standards in Wales and Scotland suffered because they didn't do the same.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: In general, education ministers in England have been more likely to set direction for teachers, highlighted by the approach to phonics.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: In Wales, for the most part, the mantra has been to trust the profession.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: And though that freedom sounds good in theory, it has pitfalls.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: It's the thinking at the heart of the new curriculum for Wales - dubbed the biggest reform to Welsh education in a generation.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: There's widespread support for the core purposes of the curriculum which aim to create well-rounded young people with the skills to contribute to the economy and to society.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: But there's less confidence in the way it tries to go about achieving that.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: The curriculum, which started being developed in 2014 and is only being fully rolled out this academic year, gives schools freedom to design their own curricula.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: In fact it's now "left almost completely up to schools what they should teach," says Lucy Crehan, an associate advisor on curriculum at Swansea University and education consultant.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Experts such as Crehan argue it's unlikely to improve standards and may make the situation worse by exacerbating inconsistency across schools.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Lucy Crehan is sceptical that the new curriculum will make things better And many teachers, already overstretched and overwhelmed, have struggled.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: "I think there does need to be more clarity for teachers, for schools on what actually it is they should be teaching and where it is they should be getting students to and by what point," Crehan says.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: She warns that it is the most disadvantaged pupils who could come off worst.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: "This is categorically not teachers' fault.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: They have been let down by a system that has said, you're the professionals, off you go and sort out everything", says Crehan.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: There has been a growing consensus about the need to provide teachers with extra support, which was acknowledged by the previous Labour government.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Teaching unions warn the profession is being asked to introduce the biggest reform to Welsh education in a generation while still dealing with the fallout of the pandemic, including poor attendance and behaviour, as well as squeezed budgets.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: In the meantime, the real test of the curriculum's impact on standards is yet to come.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: The next Pisa tests, planned for 2029, will be the first with the new curriculum fully in place.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Apart from what's taught and how, there are other factors that could influence standards.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: "There's nothing in the water in Wales that's different," says Nick Gibb.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: But, could the way the education system is structured play a part?
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Unlike in England, in Wales there are no academies or free schools.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Comprehensives, run by local authorities, are the norm.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Former First Minister Lord Carwyn Jones believes that 22 councils is too many to run education effectively.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: He says failing to cut that number is his biggest regret in government.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Jones believes there is a "structural problem in Wales where the Welsh government sets policy…but doesn't deliver education", which is the job of local authorities.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Some councils oversee a handful of schools – including only four secondaries in some cases.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: "I just don't think you can have the right level of challenge or the right level of guidance if the local authority itself is very, very small," he says.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Unless that's addressed, it's impossible "to provide the right level of support to improve our Pisa scores".
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: When Wales-based education economist Luke Sibieta compared GCSE results in areas such as Wrexham and Blaenau Gwent in Wales with the likes of similarly disadvantaged Gateshead and Salford in England, he found "disadvantaged pupils just perform worse in Wales than they do in England".
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: The latest Pisa data showed the most disadvantaged pupils in England performed above the overall Welsh average in reading.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Wales' education Minister Anna Brychan says the Pisa results are not good Reflecting on the early years of Welsh devolution, former Welsh government adviser Prof David Reynolds said ministers had been seeking change "by being nice to people rather than being nasty".
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: It's not been everyone's approach, but overall a lot of effort has been put into getting councils and unions on board with policies.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Opinions vary about whether that's served pupils and staff well.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Nick Gibb is one of those who argues that taking necessary steps to improve education standards means going "over the heads of unions" at times.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Taking the stage at Plaid Cymru's first conference in government, cabinet minister for Education Anna Brychan's assessment was more blunt than a month earlier, when the Pisa results came out.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Speaking in Welsh, she called them "brawychus" - roughly translated as "terrible" or "shocking".
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: But so far she hasn't proposed wholesale changes to education.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: The minister has been at pains to emphasise that she's committed to the new curriculum.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Even if it was practical to unpick it all, she's acknowledged there's little appetite for major upheaval.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Instead, she's promising to review aspects of it and to set clearer steps for measuring how pupils are progressing.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Brychan's view is that a focus on literacy and numeracy has been "lost in the noise" of reforms.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: She's promised more clarity.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Phonics are more central to the plan and there will be more tracking of children's progress in primary school.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Wales' education system needs to be better at measuring itself, says Luke Sibieta, who is a research fellow at the Institute for Fiscal Studies.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: And without consistent benchmarks, it's not surprising that so much weight has been placed on Pisa's verdict.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Sibieta makes the point that, looked at through a different lens, the downward trend in Wales' results is in line with "places like France, Germany, Italy, Spain" while England has been bucking the trend.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: That's little consolation for those involved in Welsh education.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Sarah Hopkins says her school has strived to build an effective curriculum due to professional pride and determination to make sure the "children get what they deserve", but she admits "there's no checks you're doing it properly".
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Overall, she is optimistic that the new curriculum and efforts in schools to improve standards will bear fruit in better Pisa scores in future.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: "I think that there will be a time where Wales will lead the way," she says.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: But some fear a generation of young people have been let down.
sentences.article_title: Wales has an education crisis. Can it be fixed?

sentences.text: Louis, Otis and Ben all have differing opinions on whether teens should use protein powder Twelve-year-old Ben is desperate to try protein powder but there's one hurdle: me, his mum.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: "I've asked about 20 times and you just keep saying no!", he says, claiming it would make him "fitter and bigger" and that his male friends use it.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: In recent years, there's been an explosion of products marketed as "high protein", including milk, yoghurt, breads, cereals, bars and powders.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Social media is flooded with adverts for various supplements, including protein powder.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: As a health journalist, I'm sceptical and think at Ben's age he must be getting enough protein through his diet.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: So, do experts think it's safe for pre-teens and teenagers or is a big, juicy steak just as good?
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: In recent years, there has been an explosion of products marketed as "high protein"... ... however, protein is found in lots of everyday foods, including meat, fish, eggs, dairy, bread, grains and pulses My sport-obsessed son, who already eats a healthy balanced diet, asks me about protein powder on a regular basis.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: His friend Louis, 12, has been using protein powder once or twice a week for nearly a year, after a workout and on top of whole foods.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: His parents are aware of this.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: "I think it's helped, it gives me more energy and it's helped me grow, probably," he says.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: But Ben's other friend Otis, who is 13, is not keen on the idea and feels there is pressure on young people to take protein supplements.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: "They might just start using them without thinking about the consequences or what effects it may have on them." Proteins break down into amino acids that help the body grow and repair.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: But your body can't make all the amino acids it needs on its own, so you need to get more - known as essential amino acids - through your diet.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: For an adult with a healthy weight, the recommended daily amount of protein you should be eating is 0.75 grams per kg of body weight, according to the NHS.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: A good rule of thumb is that the amount of protein you have for each meal should fit into the palm of your hand.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: If you exercise a lot, and when you get older, you need more protein so you could have up to 2 grams per kg of body weight.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: But do teens really need it if they're eating well?
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: This video can not be played Do you really need protein powder to build muscle?
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: For teenage boys and girls "you can get all the protein that you need from food alone", says registered dietitian Nichola Ludlam-Raine.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: It is important that teenage girls, especially, get enough iron and calcium, so Ludlam-Raine says not to become overly focused on protein at the expense of other nutrients.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Protein shakes, powders or bars can be useful for some, including high-level athletes and those who have certain allergies, but they should not replace a healthy diet.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: There can also be some unwanted side effects from using protein powders such as bloating, gas, cramps, and diarrhoea.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Those with pre-existing health conditions should not use it unless they have been told they can by their doctor.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Ludlam-Raine points out that the protein powder market is not as tightly regulated as medicines.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: "Of course, you can get reputable companies who do third-party testing and make sure that what you see on the label is what is in the inside, but that's not always the case," she says.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: "And ultimately you can't just have a shake and your biceps grow." Some protein powders contain high amounts of added sugar, artificial ingredients, and hidden stimulants.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Dr Ramnik Mathur is a consultant paediatrician from West London.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: He explains that we need micronutrients like zinc, calcium and magnesium, which are found in whole foods.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: So, if meals are replaced with protein shakes, those nutrients are lost.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Experts suggest spreading out protein across the day and aiming for 20-25g per meal.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: If you're keen to up your intake, try some of these recipes.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: During puberty when children have growth spurts, they do need more protein because their body is growing rapidly, building new muscle and bone mass.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: But Mathur says there are risks to eating too much protein.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: "If you look at social media, they'll say you need to eat a lot of protein, but your body can handle only so much." He explains that if you eat too much, it has to be excreted by the kidneys and liver which can become overloaded and have serious health implications.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: The key takeaway from Mathur: "If a 12-year-old child is eating a healthy balanced diet then they shouldn't need any more protein." Ludlam-Raine's advice is to get teens to improve their diet first before taking any protein powder, especially regularly.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: If they still want to use it, speak to a registered dietitian or nutritionist first.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Now off I go to tell my son the answer is still no - and the experts say the same.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered to take action over odours Milpitas, an affluent city in California's Silicon Valley tech hub, has an odour problem.

sentences.text: For decades, residents have had to endure rank smells wafting from industrial sites, among them a 342-acre landfill.

sentences.text: "When I first moved here, I could not open my window for over 10 years," says Chia-Ling Kong, an engineer for a tech firm who lives around half a mile from the dump.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Perhaps befitting Silicon Valley, the community is putting its hopes in technology.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Kong is optimistic a data-driven approach will make a difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Hopefully with this continuous monitoring, it makes it easier to pinpoint problems at the moment it starts." The operators of the landfill say they are committed to operating it safely and protecting air quality.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Just like in Milpitas, where Kong is part of a citizen's campaign against the odours, communities around the world are raising a stink about bad smells making day-to-day life miserable.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Sometimes a rubbish dump is to blame, or it might be a sewage treatment works, or a reeking factory.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: When the complaints start stacking up, resolving them is not always simple.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Many countries have no regulations in place dictating how to manage smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In the US, for example, the Environmental Protection Agency does not regulate environmental odours as a pollutant.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This leaves states and local governments to take charge of the issue.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Urban sprawl is often part of the problem, bringing communities closer to stinky facilities that may historically have been kept at a distance.

sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It's going to be bespoke to your farm." Apples are at least somewhat forgiving – the harvest window for those Granny Smiths is three weeks long, says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: For other fruit, such as berries, you might only have a few days.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "If a strawberry crop is on, you have to harvest it – otherwise your entire crop gets diseased very, very quickly," says Raymond Martin, co-founder and chief operating officer of FruitCast, a UK company that offers harvest forecasts to fruit growers here.

sentences.text: His firm offers growers crop predictions for strawberries and also raspberries, blackberries, blueberries and tomatoes.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Don't experienced farmers know when their fruit will be ripe, I ask?
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We do exactly what the farmers could do but we just do it on a scale that they can't." The system analyses footage of ripening fruit that can be captured by drones, someone walking up and down a field with a smartphone, or a camera mounted on a farm vehicle.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This year has been challenging, notes Martin, with hot weather and severe drought hitting much of the UK .

sentences.text: This has stressed many fruit plants, putting them into thermal dormancy and slowing down fruit production.

sentences.text: There's only a small window for picking berries says Raymond Martin The FruitCast model accounts for weather and irrigation conditions in its forecasts.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest
