sentences.text: Rainmaker's drones were used over Alaska this year On 23 August, Cooper Freeman had no idea clouds above his head were being filled with a silver compound in order to cause rainfall.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Neither did thousands of other residents in Homer, Alaska, who later discovered a  start-up called Rainmaker conducted an experiment in that region using cloud-seeding technology.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: The company, based in El Segundo California, claims it produced 19 million US gallons of water in the sky in three hours.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: This approach to weather modification, now more than 80-years-old, involves using planes and drones to disperse compounds such as silver iodide into clouds to form ice crystals.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Those crystals eventually become large enough to fall as rain or snow, depending on the temperatures below.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Essentially, cloud seeding speeds up the natural process of water vapor condensing inside of clouds.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Gravity then pulls those crystals to the ground.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: The technology, though, needs ideal climate environments, such as mountainous or cold regions such as Alaska.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Freeman, the Alaska director of the Center for Biological Diversity, isn't just concerned Homer residents weren't widely alerted to these experiments.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: He's sceptical about what was shot into the clouds, and questions how safe it was for both residents and their habitat.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "It doesn't appear that there was any downstream monitoring to verify that this silver iodide didn't impact the environment," he says.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Freeman adds, "Having a company come in to do this seeding isn't going to solve our water woes, and it feels like a distraction from solving the urgent issues related to water conservation." Concerns are mounting about the challenges surrounding water security.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres said in July "our world is using freshwater faster than it can be replenished , external ", which echoes reports noting how the past five years have led to the driest period for global rivers , external in more than three decades.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Cloud-seeding technology may be a drop in the bucket, as it doesn't create rainstorms.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: For example, Rainmaker's 19 million gallons equates to around 0.01 inch of rain across 100 square miles.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Nevertheless, more than 50 countries , external are developing programmes to modify the weather and a surge of start-ups are developing systems to create rain.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: As well developed and promising as this innovative field has become, these businesses continue to face thorny questions on safety and efficacy, leading to novel approaches with both finding the right material to spray into clouds and how they do it.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Augustus Doricko with a Rainmaker drone Augustus Doricko, the founder and CEO of Rainmaker, is quick to answer any questions on the consequences of how his company uses the silver iodide compound.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: It's clear he's been asked about chemical safety many times.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: He says Rainmaker releases this form of silver at 20 grams per flight, distributed across thousands of square kilometres.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Cloud-seeding sessions have to wait for clouds to form to try to coax them into precipitation.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Their drones are outfitted with silver iodide flares, and when lit the burning atomizes the water particles into a small enough size so they can stay suspended in the freezing cloud for hours, eventually turning into crystals and later rain.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Rainmaker operates in states such as Idaho, Utah, Colorado and areas of the Middle East such as Jordan.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: A year later, silver iodide was found to be more effective than dry ice, which quickly turns into useless gas.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: While seeding agents caused more rainfall, they didn't move the needle much.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: In fact, sobering statistics point to how patchy this technology can be in what it pours on the ground.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "With the right conditions, cloud seeding squeeze out about an extra five to 10% of precipitation," says Jon Meyer, an assistant state climatologist with the Utah Climate Center.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: What was encouraging, though, for the cloud-seeding sector was a landmark 2017 study that found how silver iodide worked as expected, one of the first reports to observe cloud seeding in action using radar and precipitation gauges.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: In the past several years, Meyer has been encouraged to see more companies such as Rainmaker bring innovation to an old industry.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "Drones [such as Rainmaker's products] present this new avenue," says Meyer, "and they offer a more targeted nature to these clouds we hope will be responsive." Olivia Li is developing an alternative to silver iodide for cloud seeding What is sprayed into clouds may also be undergoing a major shift.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Recast Systems in San Francisco is experimenting with a type of protein made from amino acids found in the soil, says CEO Olivia Li.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: While still undergoing tests at Texas A&M University, this new seeding agent moves Recast away from silver iodide as the go-to compound.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "It's safe, biodegradable and nucleates ice at a higher efficiency than silver iodide," says Li, whose company currently uses silver iodide to seed clouds in several US states.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Meyer is optimistic this technology's trajectory will only continue to rise.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "We're going to see more demand for these services as so many regions are experiencing water demand," he says, "and they're going to be looking for ways to help bridge that gap." X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Green leader Zack Polanski said the motion was 'imperfect' but supported the substance of it The equality watchdog has written to the Green Party asking for more information about a controversial "Zionism is racism" motion passed by members.
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: The Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) said it recognised that "many Jewish people will be feeling vulnerable" following the motion, passed at the party's conference earlier this month.
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: The motion described Zionism as an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state in historic Palestine to the exclusion and/or domination of the non-Jewish population".
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: In a response to the EHRC letter, the party said it "will not discriminate against or exclude people for holding Zionist views" and was committed to tackling antisemitism.
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: Dozens of Labour and Lib Dem MPs and Jewish campaigners wrote to the regulator raising concerns about antisemitism after the Green motion was passed.
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: Speaking at a press conference on Friday, author of the motion Lubna Speitan, said the Labour government had been a "participant in genocide" and had "no moral high ground to talk to us about antisemitism, racism or any other matter".
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: The International Court of Justice is currently hearing a case that accuses Israeli forces of genocide.
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: Israel has said the accusations are "wholly unfounded" and based on "biased and false claims".
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: Speitan defended her motion arguing that it was "aimed at the political ideology and practice of Zionism as defined in the motion and not the religious or ethnic background of those who may identify as Zionism".
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: "Rejecting Zionism and supporting the liberation of Palestine is not discriminatory against Jewish people," she added.
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: Alongside Jewish groups, the motion was criticised by four of the five Green MPs and two former leaders, one of whom said it was "dangerous" and "divisive".
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: It piled some pressure on Green leader Zack Polanski in the wake of a by-election defeat.
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: He said the motion was "imperfect" and he wanted to see it amended.
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: Labour has said it will end power-sharing agreements with the Greens on local councils, unless its councillors disown the motion.
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: On Thursday, the EHRC confirmed it had written to the Greens following the complaints received.
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: A spokesperson for the watchdog said: "We have written to the Green Party of England and Wales about its recently adopted 'Zionism is racism' motion to ask for more information and assess its practical implications and potential impact.
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: "We have received complaints alleging unlawful activity under the Equality Act 2010, including concerns that Jewish people could face discrimination because of their beliefs following the adoption of the motion." The watchdog said it would "take action where appropriate" after assessing the extra information.
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: "In the case of the Green Party motion, compliance with the Equality Act is likely to hinge on the practical effects of the motion," the spokesperson added.
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: In a letter earlier this month , some MPs raised concerns not only about the motion itself but also amendments to protect Jewish Green members at Zionist synagogues being voted down.
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: "Taken together, these developments raise serious questions about whether Jewish members can participate freely and equally in the party, and whether their religious and communal connections could expose them to complaints or disciplinary action," their letter said.
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: Separately, the Campaign Against Antisemitism wrote to the EHRC alleging the party had breached the Equality Act through discrimination against Jews.
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: The campaign group said the motion "effectively states that the state of Israel should not exist" and "defines support for a Jewish homeland in any form as racist".
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: Having been backed by members, the motion has become party policy but will not necessarily be included in the party's manifesto at the next general election.
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: In response to the EHRC letter, the Green Party of England and Wales said it "will not discriminate against or exclude people for holding Zionist views" and the motion sets out a political position with "no impact on membership conditions or internal disciplinary processes".
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.text: "The party's comprehensive antisemitism guidance, which forms part of our framework of ethics, remains unchanged," a spokesperson added.

sentences.text: The pedestrianisation of Oxford Street in London has been subject to much discussion The UK government has warned councils against ill-considered plans to pedestrianise high streets in England.
sentences.article_title: Councils warned of risks of high street pedestrianisation

sentences.article_title: Councils warned of risks of high street pedestrianisation

sentences.text: But the department added that "the process needs to be well considered", warning that removing traffic could make high streets less accessible and damage local economies.
sentences.article_title: Councils warned of risks of high street pedestrianisation

sentences.text: "Local leaders pursuing pedestrianisation must be aware of the risks and work to mitigate them, within a broader spatial strategy," the evidence says.
sentences.article_title: Councils warned of risks of high street pedestrianisation

sentences.article_title: Councils warned of risks of high street pedestrianisation

sentences.article_title: Councils warned of risks of high street pedestrianisation

sentences.article_title: Councils warned of risks of high street pedestrianisation

sentences.article_title: Councils warned of risks of high street pedestrianisation

sentences.article_title: Councils warned of risks of high street pedestrianisation

sentences.article_title: Councils warned of risks of high street pedestrianisation

sentences.article_title: Councils warned of risks of high street pedestrianisation

sentences.article_title: Councils warned of risks of high street pedestrianisation

sentences.text: Most pedestrianisation schemes are immediately countered by some level of local opposition, said Professor Lee Ivett, who heads the School of Architecture at the University of the Built Environment.
sentences.article_title: Councils warned of risks of high street pedestrianisation

sentences.article_title: Councils warned of risks of high street pedestrianisation

sentences.text: But he said pedestrianisation had to be paired with improvements in public transport to realise those economic benefits.
sentences.article_title: Councils warned of risks of high street pedestrianisation

sentences.text: The Brexit debate is back.

sentences.text: Little wonder perhaps that by that point, almost irrespective of someone's views on the topic, there was an appetite to talk about something else.
sentences.article_title: Why the prime minister wants to talk about Brexit again

sentences.text: Political parties picked up that vibe and while their long standing instincts on the EU were there to see if you scratched the surface, there was minimal desire to extemporise about them any time soon.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Burnham: Post-Brexit status quo with Europe 'not good enough for Britain' With the arrival of Andy Burnham as prime minister, that has changed, despite what he said just a few months before he arrived in Downing Street.

sentences.text: He has been happy to repeatedly lean into an argument claiming that it is time to "face up to the reality that Brexit has done more harm than good" and "the status quo is not good enough for Britain." First he made this case at the Labour Party Conference last month and now he has made it again in the House of Commons.

sentences.text: In the Commons, he sought to reassure you, whatever your view on Brexit.
sentences.article_title: Why the prime minister wants to talk about Brexit again

sentences.text: "This country in the next decade needs to know where it's going.

sentences.text: Trans patients should be cared for on single-sex hospital wards or bays that align with their biological sex rather than their gender identity, according to new NHS England (NHSE) guidance.

sentences.text: Previous NHSE guidance suggested patients and staff could be accommodated on wards or use facilities based on their gender identity.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The amount of time children in England spend on screens at school could be harming their "physical and developmental health", a group of more than 150 clinicians has warned.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: GPs, paediatricians and other specialists said in an open letter to Education Secretary Lucy Powell and Health Secretary Yvette Cooper that tablets and laptops are being used without a full understanding of their long-term health impacts, including on eye health.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The clinicians said they are prescribing glasses, hearing aids and speech therapy to children "for a problem that is unintentionally being made worse in our schools".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The government said it was consulting on screen time guidance for children aged five to 18 but that technology could be a powerful learning tool if used properly.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The group of clinicians said nearly one million children are using screens in most lessons, despite studies suggesting a rise in short-sightedness.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: They pointed to an analysis of 276 studies covering 5.4 million participants around the world.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: That analysis, they claimed, found a rise in short-sightedness among children and adolescents from around 24% in 1990 to almost 36% by 2023, warning the condition is associated with an increased risk of a range of eye health problems.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: She told BBC Radio 4's Today programme parents had not been given the chance to "opt out" of the "excessive" use of screens in schools, which risks children "just not thriving" in education.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: She said an "explosion" in short-sightedness "cannot be put down to genetics alone".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: It also warned that children with special educational needs are "disproportionately" directed to screen-based learning.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders, said education technology can provide schools with "very effective learning tools".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: But he said such technology was only part of an "overall learning strategy", which also includes classroom discussion and interaction, and that the school day also has  "plenty of non-screen time such as PE, sport, and break times with classmates".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: "We would welcome the development of practical, evidence-based guidance to support the work of schools in the use of education technology," he added.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: Paul Whiteman, general secretary of the National Association of Head Teachers, said it was "important that a healthy balance is struck", adding that "greater clarity is needed from the government on this".

sentences.text: Music artist Chess Galea says she no longer hides her anger Music artist Chess Galea used to suppress any feelings of anger, fearing she would be branded as "hysterical" or "difficult to work with".
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: From the "mental load" women carry to sexism in the workplace or - worse - violence against women, Galea says "we don't realise how much we accept and how much we close our mouths".
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: But now she says she simply lets it out: "If someone catcalls me in the street, I rage.
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: I don't care." From the workplace to popular culture, experts say women like Galea, 34, are increasingly expressing their anger more openly than before.
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: "The key thing is under anger there's something we care about.
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: Anger is a messenger, it brings us energy to protect, confront injustices, set boundaries, to make a change," says psychologist Dr Tara Brach.
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: What impact is that having on their professional and personal lives, and what can they do about it?
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: Jennifer Cox started to run anger processing groups for women Psychotherapist Jennifer Cox, author and co-host of the Women are Mad podcast, started researching anger after suspecting her female clients' suppression of it was the root cause of some of their physical conditions.
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: "There was this pattern of women coming in with migraines, stomach issues, musculoskeletal and immune issues.
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: Ultimately it was hard to ignore," she says.
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: "They were trying to keep their kids on track, look after their mental health and somehow do their job [too]."Cox later ran group sessions where many women let out pent-up feelings of anger.
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: "We've been brought up with this ridiculous 'good girl' stuff… indoctrinated in this idea of being good, polite, kind, thoughtful, caring," she says.
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: "The big change from previous generations is that we are expected to do it all." Brach agrees anger has its place.
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: "It becomes unhealthy when it possesses us, or when we act in ways that harm." To channel it effectively, Brach advocates mindfulness, in particular the "RAIN" strategy - recognise the emotion, allow yourself to experience it, investigate the cause, and nurture feelings of understanding.
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: Life coach Yann Dang advises women to 'build the muscle' of standing up for themselves Life coach Yann Dang, who coaches senior women in male-dominated fields, says constructive anger can actually boost women's standing in the workplace.
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: Women who people-please and don't show negative emotion can progress to a certain level on the career ladder, but to make it to the top you need to rock the boat, she argues.
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: "Women are so good at learning the rules when we know what the rules are.
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: But the rules in the corporate world are totally different." Many women know they can perform well academically so long as they work hard and prepare, she explains - but when they get to the workplace, they may struggle as attaining success is less straightforward.
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: There is little available data on female anger at work.
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: But one of the most recent in 2020 found that women expressing anger were seen as less deserving of status and influence, while their male counterparts were not.
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: The key, Dang says, is knowing how to harness that anger in a way that comes across as authentic.
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: She suggests women use direct language such as "That's a hard no for me"; "I don't like that"; and "I'm frustrated too." She also advises them to "build the muscle" of standing up for themselves, even if they don't have a perfectly polished response ready.
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: Previously, angry women characters like Alex Forrest (played by Glenn Close) in Fatal Attraction or Carrie (Sissy Spacek) in Stephen King's horror classic were unequivocally unstable and dangerous.
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: But we are increasingly seeing more positive representations of angry women in the media, says Cox, adding that these depictions are more helpful and healthy.
sentences.article_title: From the workplace to pop culture - why how we view women's anger is changing

sentences.text: Alongside everyday sexism, ongoing threats including stalking, harassment and domestic abuse serve as powerful factors uniting women in anger and defiance.

sentences.text: The NHS in England experienced its busiest September on record There are "ominous signs" that winter pressures are already affecting the NHS in England, according to senior health leaders.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: The warning comes as new data reveals the waiting list for routine hospital treatment in England rose for the second month in a row.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: An estimated 7.37 million treatments were waiting to be carried out at the end of August, relating to 6.24 million patients.

sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: The rise in waiting lists comes despite the NHS in England delivering what were described as record levels of planned, elective care over the summer, while demand for services also reached its highest level ever.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: A record 4.7 million planned treatments, procedures and appointments occurred across June, July and August – more than in any previous summer.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: But both A&Es and ambulance services also saw a record number of patients for the month of September.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: "Staff are already seeing the ominous early signs of pressure, with more patients coming to A&E with flu and other respiratory viruses than usual for this time of year, and unfortunately many people are still waiting longer than we would like them to," she said.

sentences.text: Health and Social Care Secretary, Yvette Cooper said the NHS has been dealing with summer pressures as well as winter pressures.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: "Step by step, our NHS has been increasing its delivery and performance, making a real difference to patients' lives even as demand is growing.

sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: "These are not just numbers.

sentences.text: The Institute for Government (IFG) think tank says this is partly the result of longer sentences.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: In 2023, the average prison sentence at Crown Courts in England and Wales - which deal with more serious offences - was more than 25% longer than those handed down in 2012.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: For some crimes, the increase was greater.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Sentences for robbery in 2023 were 13 months longer on average than in 2012 - an increase of 36%.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Longer sentences mean more people being held in prison at any one time.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Former Conservative Justice Secretary David Gauke, who led an independent sentencing review for Sir Keir Starmer's government, argues this is the result of a "bidding war" by political parties since the 1990s over who can imprison people for longer.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Gauke also points out that the prison population has been rising at a time when overall crime in England and Wales has been falling, according to the official Crime Survey.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: So despite the fall in crime more people are being sent to prison - and for longer.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Another reason for upward pressure on the prison population is that more people than before are being returned to prison for breaching the conditions of their release.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: There were 51,419 licence recalls in England and Wales in the year ending March 2026, up from 40,259 in the previous year - a 28% increase.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Cassia Rowland from the IFG said most recalls are for breaches of licence conditions, such as missed appointments, rather than offenders committing further offences or posing a serious risk to the public.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: "The probation service is overwhelmed, with high caseloads and lots of vacancies putting often inexperienced staff under huge pressure," she said.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Successive governments have pledged to increase the number of prison places - but delivery has often fallen short of those promises.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Between 2010 and 2024, when the Conservatives were in power, around 13,000 new prison places were created.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: But around 12,500 places - notably those built during the Victorian era - were closed after falling into disrepair.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: That means an estimated net total of only around 500 new prison places were added over 14 years.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: In a 2024 report, the National Audit Office (NAO) cited the MOJ's "unrealistic timelines", and government bodies not working together to prioritise delivery, as reasons for the slow pace of prison building.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Work is under way on a new prison - HMP Welland - being built in Leicestershire The MOJ say around 6,500 net prison places were created between 2022 and 2025, once closures are taken into consideration.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: These include places created in three new prisons.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: However, further expansion to existing prisons has been delayed by a major supplier going into administration, according to the Prison Reform Trust.

The Labour government has pledged to build 14,000 new prison places by 2031.

sentences.text: Analysts argue that without a major change in thinking about the appropriateness of prison as punishment, or a significant long-term increase in prison building, the system in England and Wales will remain close to capacity.

sentences.text: And that means governments will continue to be under pressure to implement early release schemes to avert a capacity crisis.

sentences.text: The review looks at NHS waiting times and whether young people are being over-diagnosed.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: It has been called a "generational opportunity" to rethink support for both mental health conditions and ADHD and autism.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: The review, commissioned by then-health secretary Wes Streeting 10 months ago after saying young people were being "over-diagnosed" and "written off", could have major implications for NHS services, the benefits system, schools and employment support.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Its 600-plus pages , external contain a host of conclusions and recommendations.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Here are the key takeaways.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: The report is clear that there is an increasing risk of over-diagnosis, but only when it comes to ADHD and autism.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Experts said a rise in diagnoses over the past 25 years meant cases now appear to be outstripping the expected number in the population for some younger age groups.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: They gave the example of children aged six to 17 – more than 4% have been diagnosed with autism.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: That's well above the 1-2% that studies suggest is the true level.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: But this comes with a big caveat.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: There are weaknesses in the data.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Evidence about the true level of autism relies on surveys that have not been done for nine years, so the review team have had to estimate what has happened since.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: And there are some age groups where these conditions are still being under-diagnosed, and that should not be overlooked.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: It is why the review team said it could not yet conclude over-diagnosis was happening "at scale".
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: But there is certainly evidence to suggest we are moving from an era of under-diagnosis to one of over-diagnosis, the experts said.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: They warn not every difficulty requires a medical response and there is a risk of blurring the lines between diagnosable ADHD and autism and what should be considered the "normal human variation in brain function, cognition and behaviour".
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Where the review team very clearly rejects the idea of over-diagnosis is with mental health.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: In fact, the chair, Prof Peter Fonagy, has said Streeting was "completely wrong" on that.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: He said the increase in mental distress is real – one in four 16 to 24-year-olds are now thought to experience it, up from one in six 30 years ago.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: He links this to a variety of factors including economic uncertainty, the impact of social media and loss of youth services.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: This contrasts with autism and ADHD.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: While diagnoses have increased, the true level in the whole population (regardless of whether they have come forward or not) has remained broadly stable, according to best estimates.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: What is not happening with mental health, though, is an increase in severe mental illness.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Population rates of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, for example, have remained stable.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Instead, what is driving the rise is conditions such as anxiety, depression, self-harm and eating disorders.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Where the review experts share, to some extent, Streeting's concerns is on the impact of diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: They said there was a risk it ends up closing doors to opportunities.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: It can, they said, act as a label that defines them by their "difficulties" rather than "strengths and potential".
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: This then hampers them in education, work and relationships.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Around a third of 16 to 24-year-olds not in education, employment or training (NEET) report their mental health or autism as a factor.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Those diagnosed with ADHD before the age of 17 are four times more likely to be a NEET than those without.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Addressing this, they said, would require better support post-diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Some of that is down to the NHS, but as important is the approach of schools, workplaces and wider society.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Another area where the review team is united in its view is that the support system is "falling short" of what people need for both mental health and neurological conditions such as ADHD and autism.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Waiting times for assessment are too long.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: A third of young people referred to mental health services wait more than a year, while of the 900,000 people waiting for ADHD or autism checks, 90% have waited more than three months.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: In the lead up to publication of the report, NHS Alliance, which represents health bosses, said the system was in chaos.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: But this goes further than the NHS.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: The report said support across care, education, employment and welfare remains fragmented, with people having to "jump through hoops" and face repeated assessment and conflicting requirements to get support.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: No time should be wasted in tackling these challenges, the review says.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: On long waits, it says everyone on a waiting list should be reassessed so that those most in need are prioritised for help.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: There should no longer be a first-come, first-served approach.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Some of those waiting may benefit from non-medical support, advice about sleeping better or getting more physical exercise, for example.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: That may even lead to some being removed from the waiting list.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: There should also be better assessments before people are placed on waiting lists too.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Not every problem needs a medical solution, the experts make clear.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Quality and consistency of autism and ADHD assessments must be improved, with the review highlighting concerns about those done by the private sector on behalf of the NHS.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Half of ADHD and a third of autism assessments are done by non-NHS providers, such as charities and private firms.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: But they are not subject to the same regulation as NHS providers – and this must change.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: The experts also said it wanted to see a ban on direct-to-public advertising of assessments.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: The review has said it wants to see action over the next 12 to 24 months.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: The government has promised to act – and is expected to set out more details in its forthcoming mental health strategy which is expected by the end of the year.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Antonia says she wants to remain open about her health to inspire other women in business When Antonia Okonma Shittu was told she had multiple sclerosis (MS) and would be using a wheelchair within the year, she was in denial.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: The 26-year-old, who was in between acting jobs and working in a call centre, said the diagnosis was a "massive turning point" in her life.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: "It does really make you think about what you want to do in life," she said.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: She looked back to what she enjoyed doing as a child - styling hair - and decided to use the shock of the diagnosis to spur her on to turn her passion into a business.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: Antonia, who grew up on a council estate in west London, bought two wigs and went door to door selling them from the boot of her car.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: Antonia with American actress Niecey Nash Almost two decades later, she is now a multi-million-pound brand owner, with current and past high-profile clients including tennis icon Serena Williams, actress Niecey Nash and model Naomi Campbell.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: She even won a Black British Business Award last week .
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: Antonia, now 44, still struggles with her health, having also received diagnoses of Graves' disease - an autoimmune condition - and heart failure, but hopes her experience running a hair empire while fitting in hospital appointments can inspire other women.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: Antonia says she saw a gap in the market when she was surrounded by "terrible" wigs while working in TV and film, including in the ITV series Bad Girls two decades ago.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: "Women wanted natural-looking wigs and they just weren't available.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: They looked like helmets!" Antonia set up a Facebook page and began advertising on Gumtree.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: "I had very limited resources.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: I didn't have any investors behind me.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: I come from very humble beginnings." Her experience dealing with MS has helped her success, she says.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: Antonia lost her hair when she underwent chemotherapy following a bone marrow transplant, so she knows what it is like to be "completely bald".
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: This made her relate more deeply to her customers, she explains, as she understands the loss of control some women feel when they lose their hair.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: "I didn't feel like myself," she says, "but being able to put on a wig that looks something close to how your hair was, or the look you used to have, it's as though you can feel like yourself again." When she sees a woman put a wig on and her "whole face lights up", it can be "very, very rewarding".
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: "When we feel good about ourselves...we're more confident, we can achieve more.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: I felt like I was changing the world, one person at a time." Antonia experienced hair loss after undergoing chemotherapy While Antonia's business, A-List Lace Hair, has grown from strength to strength, with salons in London and New York, she has been dealing with the impact of her health conditions.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: She struggles with fatigue due to her MS and uses a wheelchair, but says this has not stopped her success.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: Instead, it has simply changed the way she has run her business.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: "I used to feel that being a good entrepreneur was being able to do as much as I can myself," Antonia said.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: "Due to my health challenges, there are days where I literally can't feel my legs, they feel like jelly, there's days where I'm completely exhausted after sleeping, I wake up completely shattered." This has forced her to "trust other people and gain strength in building a team".
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: As a woman in business, being in a wheelchair can sometimes make Antonia feel "smaller" as people often have to look down at her at industry events.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: "People are often surprised when I start speaking about my business, as though they're thinking 'how have you accomplished all of this in a wheelchair?'" Antonia, who has three young children, says that being underestimated can be a good thing, and she wants to remain open about her health to inspire other women.
sentences.article_title: I lost my hair to chemo - now my wigs are worn by A-list stars

sentences.text: She says she used to feel "weak" because of her disability, but now feels she has gained "so much strength" from sharing her experience online.

sentences.text: Asked what she would say to another woman who may fear her age, disability or health could get in the way of success, she says: "I would encourage them to just start." sentences.text: Have you ever slept next to a snoring partner and woken up feeling stressed, unfocused or forgetful the next day?
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: As snoring is relatively common, it is often left untreated and dismissed as a harmless irritation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But according to experts, sleeping next to a snorer could be impacting your health.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Snoring is caused by the vibration of the soft tissues in our upper airways during sleep, explains Dr Clare Simon, a dentist with a special interest in dental sleep medicine.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: About 40% of the UK adult population snores, with the issue affecting more men than women, says the British Snoring and Sleep Apnoea Association (BSSAA).
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: And 75% of people with a snoring partner say they have had their sleep impacted, according to a US survey by the Sleep Foundation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know about the impact on partners - and what you can do about it.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Prof Ama Johal, a consultant orthodontist and sleep expert at Aerox Health, explains that the partner of a snorer can become "so impacted upon that it's almost a last-ditch effort on their part to get up and go sleep in a separate room because they have to sleep".
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: He adds: "As humans we physically can't function without that necessity." Prof Ama Johal says many couples put up with the negative effects snoring for too long During the night, we cycle through different stages of sleep in repeating patterns, usually every 90 minutes.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: The deeper stages of this cycle are important for physical restoration.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: If sleep is frequently disrupted, you may spend less time in the restorative stages, meaning you can wake up feeling tired, even if you've spent a lot of time in bed, the BSSAA explains.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Your brain processes and stores information from the day during sleep.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Fragmented sleep - which can happen if you're waking up due to a snoring partner - can interrupt this process, impacting your focus and memory.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Disrupted sleep can also impact hormone regulation, which affects your energy levels and motivation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Sleep also plays a role in regulating the brain systems involved in stress and emotional response.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: When it is disrupted, these systems can become less balanced, which may make you feel more irritable and less able to cope with stress.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: This is something Meg Warren, 29, experienced when her former partner's snoring would keep her up.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says: "Without fail, after a snoring-induced wake up I would feel on incredibly high alert." Meg, a charity media officer, would prod him throughout the night and try to coax him from his back to his side.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says she would wake up "feeling groggy and dazed, sometimes so much so that it would feel like a hangover".
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Meg Warren felt 'groggy and dazed' after a night of little sleep due to her former partner's snoring Anna-Louise Dearden, a 52-year-old journalist, says she sometimes sleeps in a separate room from her partner due to his snoring.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Having this option allows her to prioritise getting enough rest when the snoring is particularly bad.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: There are things that can be done, say both Simon and Johal.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But first, it is important to distinguish whether your partner is simply snoring, or whether they have sleep apnoea.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: "What you don't want to do is simply make someone quieter at night while potentially missing an underlying sleep-related breathing disorder," Simon says.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Signs of sleep apnoea, a disorder that causes a person's breathing to repeatedly stop and start during sleep, include pauses in breathing, choking at night, waking frequently, and suffering from morning headaches.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: If this is what you are dealing with, you could be recommended a Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) machine, or even surgical treatment in some cases, Simon explains.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: For simple snoring, Simon said that lifestyle changes can make a difference, such as losing weight, stopping smoking, reducing alcohol intake before bed, or changing your sleeping position - such as laying on your side rather than your back.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: You can also suggest to your partner that they see a GP, who will be able to advise further or refer you to a specialist.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: An expert might suggest treating nasal obstruction or allergies, if this is what is causing snoring, or wearing a custom mouthguard to gently push the lower jaw forward and keep the airway open.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Johal says too many couples put up with snoring "for too long", which impacts their relationships and wellbeing.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Sarah Mackay, known as @fitwsarah online, says her energy levels change through her cycle A woman points to a colour-coded grid dividing the menstrual cycle into four phases, each paired with a different list of exercises.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "When you're bleeding, you want to be doing steady-pace jogging, Pilates, barre, walking, resting," she tells viewers.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: This is one of thousands of videos on TikTok and Instagram suggesting that people change their workouts depending on where they are in their menstrual cycles - something known as 'cycle-syncing'.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: So-called cycle-syncing workout plans have surged in popularity online, with Google searches for the term rising 740% since 2022 and more than 55,000 TikTok videos now using the #cyclesyncing hashtag.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Most of the advice is shared by fitness and wellness creators rather than medical or research experts.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Kelly McNulty, a researcher at Leeds Beckett University specialising in menstrual cycles and exercise, says there is evidence that some women experience changes in symptoms, energy or perceived strength across their cycle.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But that is different from evidence that all women should train in a particular way at a particular point, she tells the BBC, adding that these videos are "a trend based on marketing rather than any kind of research or evidence".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "There isn't any research to support that kind of phase-based prescription," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: This video can not be played Should you sync your exercise routine with your period?
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: A key issue is that menstrual cycles are highly individual, McNulty adds - they can differ between women, and one woman's experience can also change from one cycle to the next.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: That makes the blanket advice often found on social media difficult to apply, she explains.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Many cycle-tracking apps and programmes are also designed around relatively regular menstrual cycles that are 21 to 35 days, which can make their recommendations less applicable to people with irregular periods, or those using hormonal contraception.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She doesn't follow a prescriptive plan, she says, but instead makes changes intuitively.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my luteal phase I'll try and ease off in the training," she tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my follicular phase, I'm so energised, I feel like I can lift so much heavier.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: I like to try and get my long runs in." Burgoyne also welcomes the growing attention on women's health, and says that exercise and nutrition research has historically focused heavily on male bodies, with findings then often applied to women.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Sarah says she has sometimes hit personal records while on her period Fitness creator Sarah Mackay, known as @liftwsarah on Instagram and TikTok, has also noticed her energy, motivation, cramps and mood change through the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But she deliberately avoids strict plans because, she says, "there are too many variables at play".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Some online plans advise women to avoid intense training during their period, she says, yet she has sometimes hit personal records while menstruating.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "The problem is not that the menstrual cycle is irrelevant," she says, but that "not everything is predictable".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Dr Faye Bate, a trained medical doctor and women's health expert, is also wary of advice suggesting all women should train differently according to their menstrual phase.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "A one-size-fits-all model of 'you should be exercising this way in this phase and a different way in a different phase' shouldn't be advice that applies to all women," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She is concerned that repeatedly telling women they are likely to be weaker or less capable at particular points in their cycle could create a "nocebo" effect - where negative expectations themselves influence how someone feels or performs.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty tells the BBC that routinely easing off resistance training could also limit progress.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Strength training is particularly important for women, who face a higher risk of osteoporosis later in life.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: While cycle-syncing itself may not be backed by strong evidence, the experts we spoke to did suggest being "cycle-aware".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty says tracking your cycle can be a useful way to understand your own patterns, while Dr Bate also encourages women to become more familiar with how they feel at different points in the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Both welcome the fact that menstrual health is being discussed more openly, but say the focus should be on individual experience, rather than rigid, phase-based rules.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In practice, that might mean having painkillers ready before your period, taking a rest day when symptoms are worse, or easing off a workout if you feel unusually fatigued.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: For Dr Bate, "the most important part is tuning in to how you feel".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In other words, use your cycle as information rather than a set of rules.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: The Happy Mums Foundation was set up in Carlisle in 2015 by a mum who experienced isolation after being treated in a Psychiatric Mother and Baby Unit A charity has said it is "terrified" new mums suffering from suicidal thoughts will be left with nowhere to turn if its group sessions end due to funding pressures.
sentences.article_title: Charity 'terrified' closure could leave mums suicidal

sentences.text: The Happy Mums Foundation, which supports women experiencing postpartum mental health challenges, was set up in 2015 and has helped more than 1,000 families across Cumbria.
sentences.article_title: Charity 'terrified' closure could leave mums suicidal

sentences.text: Charity director Lucinda Bray fears the loss of the in-person "safe place" could worsen the mental health of vulnerable women in the county.
sentences.article_title: Charity 'terrified' closure could leave mums suicidal

sentences.text: Women who have attended the sessions say the charity, which would move online only, offers "no judgement" peer support and helps mums feel less isolated when experiencing trauma.
sentences.article_title: Charity 'terrified' closure could leave mums suicidal

sentences.text: Bray said: "I'm terrified, if we don't have in-person groups for mums, where will they go?
sentences.article_title: Charity 'terrified' closure could leave mums suicidal

sentences.text: "The long nights, the crying and not knowing what it is they want, you've just been handed a tiny human being and you're meant to just know what to do and having the expectations of mum knows best.
sentences.article_title: Charity 'terrified' closure could leave mums suicidal

sentences.text: "I didn't have a clue and I think a lot of mums are in the same boat." At first Amy found it difficult to leave the house with her daughter who was born prematurely.
sentences.article_title: Charity 'terrified' closure could leave mums suicidal

sentences.text: Now, she attends the charity's teen to 25 group, which has helped her build confidence.
sentences.article_title: Charity 'terrified' closure could leave mums suicidal

sentences.text: "Obviously everyone absolutely adores the babies here but it's called Happy Mums for a reason," she said.
sentences.article_title: Charity 'terrified' closure could leave mums suicidal

sentences.text: "There's plenty of support out there for babies, but it's nice to have something that is more about the mums." Amy said without the support of the group she would struggle more to get out and about.
sentences.article_title: Charity 'terrified' closure could leave mums suicidal

sentences.text: "When I'm feeling low with my depression or anxiety and more anxious about going out I know that I can come to Happy Mums, I look forward to it," she said.
sentences.article_title: Charity 'terrified' closure could leave mums suicidal

sentences.text: The group says over the last year funding for preventative mental health services has become increasingly difficult to secure.
sentences.article_title: Charity 'terrified' closure could leave mums suicidal

sentences.text: Bray said the 13 weekly support groups have already been reduced to five, and without investment the charity will be forced to move groups online or close completely.
sentences.article_title: Charity 'terrified' closure could leave mums suicidal

sentences.text: Growing financial pressures across the charities sector has been evident in recent months, including the closure of suicide prevention charity Papyrus in September.
sentences.article_title: Charity 'terrified' closure could leave mums suicidal

sentences.text: Cumbria has a limited number of groups offering the type of support available through Happy Mums National Council for Voluntary Organisations' chief influencing officer Leigh Brimicombe said the current financial climate was "tough" for charity organisations.
sentences.article_title: Charity 'terrified' closure could leave mums suicidal

sentences.text: He said the cost of living crisis meant there was a "growing need for support in communities but also less money available for donors or funders to give, compounded by increased running costs for charities themselves".
sentences.article_title: Charity 'terrified' closure could leave mums suicidal

sentences.text: Labour MP for Penrith and Solway, Markus Campbell-Savours, sent a letter of concern about the future of foundation to the Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear NHS Trust.
sentences.article_title: Charity 'terrified' closure could leave mums suicidal

sentences.text: In reply, chief executive James Duncan said "peer-led and community-based support can form a valuable part of the wider network for support available to women and families".
sentences.article_title: Charity 'terrified' closure could leave mums suicidal

sentences.text: He added although formal joint working with the NHS was not possible due to the distinction between peer-led and clinical services, the potential closure was "particularly concerning given the relatively limited number of voluntary and community sector organisations providing this type of support across Cumbria".
sentences.article_title: Charity 'terrified' closure could leave mums suicidal

sentences.text: The Department of Health and Social Care has been approached for comment.
sentences.article_title: Charity 'terrified' closure could leave mums suicidal
