sentences.text: Liberty York died aged 19, a year after she first experienced symptoms of an angiosarcoma Liberty York was 19 when she died from a rare form of cancer, two days after her birthday.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: A year after her death, her mother Hannah York has talked about her strength and the parts of her daughter that existed outside of her illness.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: "The first thing that comes to mind when I think about Liberty is how kind she was and thoughtful," she said.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: To Hannah, she was still the same determined teenager throughout the final year of her life, before she died from an angiosarcoma, a rare form of soft tissue sarcoma, a type of cancer which starts in areas of the body such as muscle and fat.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: The first signs appeared in May 2024 when Liberty, from Stratford-upon-Avon, Warwickshire, began feeling unusually tired and nauseous.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: A year earlier she had been diagnosed with Addison's disease, a rare autoimmune condition, so at first the family thought it was possible the two could be linked.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: Liberty was referred to see a specialist but while the family waited for answers, she developed swelling and pain in her left breast.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: "We went to see the GP about the swelling and she thought it was mastitis because it was red as well and painful.," Hannah said.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: "The [cancer's]  main symptom is the swelling or change in skin.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: Liberty's swelling kept getting bigger and bigger." Antibiotics were prescribed but they failed to work and doctors initially thought she had an abscess.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: Liberty was remembered as being strong and kind by her mother Hannah Later, Hannah said, attention turned towards the possibility that hormones could be responsible.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: "Liberty was on a teenage cancer ward and they said it was very common," she said.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: "So many teenagers, it's put down to hormones and unfortunately they said they see it every day." The swelling that had begun as a small area of concern just weeks earlier had become a tumour weighing 10lb (4.5kg) by the time surgery took place.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: For Hannah, that moment brought relief that they finally had an answer, but also the harsh reality of what her daughter was facing.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: "Liberty's type of sarcoma was a particularly aggressive sarcoma and, after she was operated on, it had spread to her lungs in just six weeks," she remembered.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: "The difference between days and weeks to diagnosis is so important with sarcoma.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: She didn't get a fighting chance." Liberty died in the early hours of 1 June 2025, two days after celebrating her 19th birthday.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: Hannah hoped more early diagnoses will help other teenagers beat the disease In the months since, Hannah said she had tried to channel her grief into raising awareness of the disease that took her daughter.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: She is supporting the Child Cancer Smart campaign, led by CCLG: The Children & Young People's Cancer Association, as it launches new guidelines for healthcare professionals, aimed at improving recognition of soft tissue sarcomas in children and young people.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: These cancers account for about  7% of childhood cancers, according to the charity, but experts say diagnosis can often be delayed because symptoms resemble more common conditions.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: "Liberty was an incredibly strong person with a very strong sense of right and wrong.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: She was very opinionated, which I loved about her," Hannah said.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: "I don't know if any earlier diagnosis could have saved her, but she'd have had more of a chance.
sentences.article_title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis

sentences.text: There is a risk of people being over-diagnosed with ADHD and autism, an official review in England has found.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: Experts said a rise in diagnoses over the past 25 years meant cases now appear to be outstripping the expected number in the population for some younger age groups.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: The review called for tougher regulation of private firms offering assessments for the NHS, saying they had concerns about quality and consistency, and a ban on advertising.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: It concluded economic uncertainty combined with social media was driving an increase in mental health problems among young people and said there needed to be better support in place for all conditions.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: The review - led by leading doctors in the field - was ordered 10 months ago by Wes Streeting after the then-health secretary claimed in an interview that young people were over-diagnosed and "written off".
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: It looked at people of all ages, but particularly focused on young people and children who have the highest rates of diagnoses.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: It is likely to feed into government policies on everything from NHS services and benefits to support for young people who are not in education, employment or training.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: The experts said too often diagnoses of mental health problems and ADHD and autism were ending up as labels that defined people by their "difficulties rather than their strengths and potential", harming their prospects at school, in work and in relationships.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: Children diagnosed with autism and ADHD before the age of 17 are around four times more likely to end up not in education, employment or training between 16 and 24.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: With better support after diagnosis, they could be helped to live more fulfilling lives, the review said.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: Alongside access to therapies, this should also include support for mental health – significant numbers also struggle with conditions such as depression.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: But the review found people were also being harmed by long waits for diagnosis for mental health and ADHD and autism.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: The Watsons are just one family who have experience of this.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: Ryan and his wife knew there was something different with their son Atlas when he was around 12 to 18 months old and missing development milestones.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: But it took three years to get an autism assessment.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: As time passed, his needs became increasingly clear.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: Now nearly seven, Atlas is non-verbal, still wears nappies and relies on others for all aspects of daily care.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: Despite this, Ryan said there was no fast-track route for children with the most complex needs.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: "You basically go on the list and wait however long until you get to the top." The wait left the family racing against time to secure support before Atlas started school.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: Ryan and his wife feared he would be placed in a mainstream school.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: "We were terrified," Ryan says.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: "Anyone who has a child like Atlas will have the same panic that they'll start in a mainstream school where it's not safe." The strain was immense.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: "It was like I had two jobs," Ryan says.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: "I was going to work and then coming home and dealing with these things." Atlas was eventually diagnosed only months before starting school.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: This could include adjustments being made at school or in workplaces and lifestyle support, such as help to improve sleep or address anxiety, it said.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: Too often, access to help requires a diagnosis, with experts highlighting changes in 2014 that required parents to get a diagnosis of autism and ADHD to qualify their children for extra support in schools.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: Review chair Prof Peter Fonagy said it was clear the system was "under immense strain" and it was time to get away from diagnosis being a "very narrow pathway" to finding support.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: It said there was a risk society was now moving from an era of under-diagnosis to over-diagnosis or mis-diagnosis, pointing to data showing more than 4% of children aged six to 17 were now diagnosed with autism, well above the 1-2% that studies suggest is the true level.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: But it said because some of these figures date back nearly a decade it was not possible to be absolutely certain or conclude over-diagnosis was currently occurring at scale.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: And there are some age groups where these neurological conditions are still being under-diagnosed – and that should not be over-looked either, it added.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: Mel Merritt, of the National Autistic Society, said the report shows that successive governments "have failed autistic people".
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: "The harm and distress autistic people are facing is real and widespread and there is a desperate need to build a system that supports the needs of autistic people." Abigail Ampofo, of charity YoungMinds, said: "For years, young people have told us they feel blamed for their mental health or accused of making it up.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: We hope this review goes some way to show them their distress is not their fault and the systems around them are failing." But she said that would require major reform.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: The government welcomed the publication of the report and said it would be setting out a new model of providing support in its forthcoming mental health strategy, which is expected before the end of the year, and also promised to introduce tougher regulation of ADHD and autism assessments.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: Now NHS needs to change' When Poppy Russell died shortly after birth, her parents were left bereft.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: What followed made matters harder to bear - her mother was blamed for the death.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: An inquest would later conclude that Poppy's death was preventable.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: But instead of walking away from the trust that had failed them, Neil and Katie Russell are now working with it to bring compassionate care back into the NHS.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: "We could have very easily been consumed by hate and anger and rage at what happened – and those feelings are still there," said Katie.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: "But if no change comes from what happened to Poppy, then what's the point?" Neil and Katie Russell are working with the hospital where their daughter died Poppy Russell died in April 2021 at the Princess Royal Hospital in Telford.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: She was just 12 hours old.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: During her pregnancy her mother told midwives that she had tokophobia, a fear of natural birth and wanted a caesarean section.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: Katie said she was repeatedly told however that she "couldn't just ask for a c-section." When she went into labour, Katie was induced and then "we were left in a room for long periods of time where I had no care," she explained.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: "Finally, when we got into the labour suite, I wasn't monitored appropriately and they missed signs that Poppy was in distress." In a bitter irony, Poppy had to be delivered by emergency caesarean.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: By then however, she had developed a hypoxic brain injury and died later the same day.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: An inquest into her death found that had Poppy been born an hour earlier, she would have survived .
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: The Shrewsbury and Telford NHS Trust (SaTH), which ran the hospital, subsequently blamed Katie for her daughter's death.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: They said she had refused foetal monitoring; the inquest concluded that was untrue.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: "The trust left us in an appalling position," said Neil Russell.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: "Not only were they found to have neglected our care, but in the months and years following, we uncovered that members of staff had tried to cover it up.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: In March 2024, the couple had a meeting with the trust to discuss all that had happened.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: From the discussions, Neil and Katie decided they needed to honour Poppy.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: "The first conversations about Poppy's Promise were about being human," said Neil, 45.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: For matcha fans, the drink contains more caffeine than a cup of tea but less than a regular coffee.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You could structure your day differently too, and take a southern European approach to eating.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Have an early breakfast, an afternoon siesta while it's very hot and then a late dinner.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A second head teachers' union has called for a halt to graded Ofsted inspections in England, saying it is "increasingly concerned about the welfare and morale" of its members.

sentences.text: Ofcom is investigating whether Meta breached its duties under the UK's online safety laws with the launch of its "Instants" feature on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: The tool - allowing users to take and share an instant image with close friends, that disappears once viewed - was launched on Meta's photo-sharing app in May as "a new way to share photos in the moment".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But the regulator said the social media giant had not properly assessed risks posed by the feature prior to launching it - something it is required to do under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA).
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said in a statement that it "takes its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Under the UK's sweeping online safety rules, platforms including Meta must carry out and update risk assessments to comply with a range of duties, including to tackle illegal content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: They must also show how they prevent children permitted to use their services from encountering content deemed harmful for them.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: This spans material relating to pornography, or promoting self-harm or suicide - as "priority primary content" - alongside things like abusive, hateful or bullying content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Our online safety laws are clear – significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched," said Ofcom enforcement director George Lusty.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "This is a vital step that tech firms must take to protect their users," he added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Images shared with Instants can be viewed by those who have been selected as "close friends" by a user, or those who they follow and are followed back by.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta says the feature has a range of built-in protections, including for younger users with Teen Accounts, including preventing screenshots, reshares or forwarding of Instants.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But disappearing messages and images have been singled out previously as posing particular risks for child or teen users of some apps .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Safety by design must be built in, not bolted on, and today's investigation shows we'll take action where we have concerns that providers are failing to comply," Lusty added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: All three companies have appeared in court this week, arguing they should not need to provide so much information in response to Ofcom's formal requests.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta has separately also argued Ofcom should not be able to levy fines for breaches based on its global annual revenue.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: It also contends that its messaging and image-sharing apps should not have to face additional requirements under the OSA, such as tackling paid-for fraud ads.

sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Milburn told the BBC "in primary school, it's really about opening their eyes and giving them a sense about what is possible".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Despite a push towards apprenticeships and work experience in Years 10 and 11, for many the journey towards becoming Neet starts well before their 16th birthday.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: As a result, Milburn says children should be introduced to the world of work much earlier in their school journey, with dedicated space in the curriculum to "broaden horizons".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The final instalment of Alan Milburn's review into Neets is due to be published this autumn He told the BBC this could be achieved by employers giving talks in primary schools and offering taster sessions to children.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "It'd be good if employers came into schools and said, 'Look, this is what's going on, these are things that are possible.'" Milburn says that for Key Stage 4 pupils - aged between 14 and 16 - experience must be given in a real workplace with employer feedback.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Work experience needs to be mandatory.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: It makes a big difference," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Milburn also emphasised the difficulty some young people face when trying to find work experience placements.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "There are about four in ten people aged 14-16 who aren't getting any work experience at all," he said.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Education is devolved in the UK, so while Milburn's review looks at the picture in all four nations, his recommendations regarding education are specific to England.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Currently in England, careers guidance must be offered to students aged 11-18 and work experience is not statutory.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The government has said its vision , external is to "guarantee two weeks' worth of work experience for every young person" in England.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: In both Scotland and Wales, career-based learning is already a requirement in schools for students as young as three.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Emma, from Kirklees, has grandchildren in Years 1, 2 and 4 and thinks primary school is too young to be introducing careers talks.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "In primary school, there is too much trying to get little kids to grow up too quickly," she says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Just let them be little kids.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: I know they have to learn and the world's changing, but still, give them a chance to be kids." But Zoe, another parent, disagrees.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "I think it's a good idea," she says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Whenever new mandatory requirements are proposed, it is important to be clear about what might have to give way to make room for them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: WhatsApp is introducing new parental controls for teenagers, as tech companies continue to come under pressure to provide more age-appropriate experiences for children.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The social messaging app's new tools will give parents a range of options, such as being told when their child joins or leaves a group.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It will also let them decide on privacy settings for their account.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In a blog post, WhatsApp, clarified parents would not be given the power to see the messages their teen is sending and receiving, which along with calls would stay private and protected by end-to-end encryption.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And it said the controls were optional, which social media analyst Matt Navarra called an "obvious weakness".
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: He said the move was "fairly convenient" for Meta, which owns WhatsApp, because it reduced the company's reliance on age verification by putting some responsibility on parents and teenagers.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "Meta is trying to show regulators we have a child safety system, we have parental controls and we're rolling it out across our platforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "I think the big unanswered question is whether enough families will actually use it." The minimum age to use WhatsApp is 13 in the UK, although it is higher in some countries.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: According to the firm, parents will be able to adjust or switch off the controls at any time.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The settings will be "straightforward to set up" using a Pin set by a parent, which teens will need if they want to switch off the controls.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Some of the new privacy tools include selecting who can see a child's profile photo and who can add them to groups.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Parents can also choose how their teenager uses Channels, which allows organisations and public figures to send out content.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And they will have the option of choosing between the default 13+ setting for Meta AI, the app's optional built-in AI assistant, or a stricter "Limited Content" option.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "All of these controls are being designed to support open conversations about how to use WhatsApp between parents and teens, while keeping everyone's personal messages private," the company said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The changes come as pressure mounts on tech companies from governments and regulators to change the way they operate in order to better protect children using their platforms.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In June, the government announced it plans to ban under-16s from social media platforms, with the restrictions expected to come into force in March 2027.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It said "highly effective age assurance" measures would be used to check the age of those using social media.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: WhatsApp is currently excluded from the ban because the government considers it a messaging service.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Cases of antisemitism affecting university students and staff in the UK increased in the last academic year, according to a charity that monitors antisemitic incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The Community Security Trust (CST) said it had recorded 95 "university-related" incidents in the 2025-26 academic year - up from 83 the year before.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said the number had fallen from its peak in the year after Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023 and the war in Gaza began, but remains "substantially higher" than before that point.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Universities UK (UUK) represents more than 140 institutions and said its members needed to "protect Jewish students and staff", adding that the findings were a "serious concern".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Lucy Powell, education secretary in England, said the findings in the CST report were "deeply troubling".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: "We expect universities to take a zero-tolerance approach to antisemitism, and are providing training to help university staff identify and respond to incidents swiftly," she said.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The CST defines an antisemitic incident as "university-related" if it concerns a student, member of staff or academic at a UK university "in their academic or student capacity" - including on campus and online.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: In 2022-23, the last academic year before the 7 October attack, the CST recorded 53 incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: That grew to 272 in 2023-24.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: A report from the charity examining the past two academic years says reported incidents fell in 2024-25 and but grew again in 2025-26.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The most common type of incident recorded by CST over both years was abusive behaviour, including verbal abuse, comments made in person or online and antisemitic graffiti.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Its report said that, for the first time, there were two occurrences of extreme violence in 2024-25.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said there were six reported assaults across both years, eight incidents of damage and desecration to Jewish property - five of which were in student accommodation - and ten threats.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Around two-thirds of reported incidents involved antisemitic language or targeting alongside references to Israel, Gaza, Hamas, the 7 October attack, and the subsequent conflicts in the Middle East.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The war in Gaza was triggered by the Hamas attack on Israel on 7 October 2023 in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others taken hostage.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Israel launched a mass military offensive on Gaza in response which has killed around 74,000 people, according to the Hamas-run health ministry.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: He added that universities had "a duty to ensure that Jewish students and staff can study, work and participate on campus the same as anyone else".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Raphi Leon, president of the Union of Jewish Students, said the report "must be a shot in the arm to boost action to support Jewish students and tackle antisemitism".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Vivienne Stern, chief executive of UUK, said: "The rise in antisemitic incidents in the UK, including on university campuses, is a serious concern.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Experts warn children as young as five years old are now being groomed on social media and gaming sites Experts are urging parents to talk to their children amid warnings social media grooming is becoming "quicker" and "easier" than ever before.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Childline said Snapchat, TikTok and Instagram were the top platforms children named in counselling about online sexual abuse last year.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: The companies have been approached for comment.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Avon and Somerset Police's child exploitation prevention officer Andri Nicolau said children as young as five can be targeted through social media, gaming and messaging platforms.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: She urged parents to encourage kids to ask for help without fear of blame or punishment.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: The warning comes after three men were jailed for grooming a 17-year-old girl on Snapchat before raping her.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Research by the NSPCC found sexual communication offences involving children in the South West have more than doubled since the offence was introduced seven years ago, to 756 in 2024/25.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Of those, 300 were recorded by Avon and Somerset Police, 96 by Gloucestershire Constabulary and 61 by Wiltshire Police.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: The charity also said Snapchat was mentioned in 324 counselling sessions about online sexual abuse between April 2025 and March 2026, a 19% increase on the previous year.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: TikTok (234) and Instagram (197) were the next most frequently mentioned platforms.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Chris Sherwood, chief executive of the NSPCC, said: "It's deeply disturbing that hundreds of children have come to us in the past year alone, disclosing experiences of online sexual abuse linked to these popular apps and platforms.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Aqeel used social media, including Snapchat, to arrange to meet young girls.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: He also filmed some of his offences and threatened to share intimate videos and images.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: New data suggests that this particular form of exploitation of children, known as 'sextortion', has also reached record levels.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: The Internet Watch Foundation (IWF) said there has been a sharp rise in the number of young people contacting its confidential Report Remove helpline , external because they fear sexual images of themselves have been shared, or could be shared, online.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Criminals try to extort or blackmail their victims by threatening to publish the images, which have often been taken by the child themselves.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Nicolau said children spending more time online meant they were increasingly vulnerable to grooming, which is "easier" and "quicker" than ever before.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "With online gaming and social media, you have kids from five years old online, some of them have their own phones, so it can be any age," she said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: She works with schools to inform children how to be safe online, but said they are often unaware of the risks, including not viewing people they meet online as strangers and expecting them to be "nasty" from the start.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Nicolau encouraged any child or young person who believes they are being groomed to "find someone they are comfortable with and speak to them".
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: She said the police might not be the first choice, but speaking to somebody they trust is what mattered.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Sit down with your child, tell them it's not their fault, even if they've sent indecent images of themselves," she said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: The Exmoor Dark Skies festival celebrates its 10th anniversary in 2026 Stargazers and astronomers are preparing to enjoy a festival that celebrates the beauty of the night sky.
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: The annual Exmoor Dark Skies Festival is being held from 16 October to 1 November and this year is its 10th anniversary.
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: Taking in villages and towns surrounding Exmoor National Park, the event offers walks, talks and shows - putting the dark, clear, night sky into full focus.
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: Granted by the International Astronomical Union in 2011, the status aims to safeguard the right of any citizen to enjoy the night sky by helping to limit light pollution.
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: Photographers and astronomers can enjoy clear views of the stars during the festival Colman said there is "very little light pollution on Exmoor", adding it "enables the dark to be really dark with none of the pollution impacting".
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: "In the core of the reserve, there's an area where there is no light at all in a huge area - and that just makes the sky so much clearer and you're able to see some incredible constellations.
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: "You can see the Milky Way - it really is fantastic." Photographs taken during previous dark skies events show incredibly clear views of the stars against a clear, dark backdrop.
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: Locations such as Wimbleball Lake are big draws The National Park said it designed the event in 2017 to, in part, help local businesses towards the end of the traditional tourism season.
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: In Dunster, on the edge of Exmoor, the Yarn Market Hotel manager Antony Brunt said in recent years, "it has become much more widely known - and now we literally have people ringing us up to book".
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: The hotel hosts special trips during the festival, led by a local astronomer, and runs visits to various sites and events across the park.
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: Brunt said the festival brings in people from all over the UK, adding: "It's getting to a quieter time of year and these people, they really enjoy coming down.
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: "We have a group that come each year, in fact, twice a year.
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: For people to come regularly twice a year to the same hotel, they must be enjoying the stargazing part of the weekend." The growing popularity of the festival meant that many events sold out before the opening day.
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: Lizzy, Charlotte and Libby studied at the University of Newcastle between 2012 and 2015 When Lizzy, Libby and Charlotte met as freshers in 2012, their main responsibility was making it to lectures on time after early morning sports practice.

sentences.text: Their student debt, growing with interest from the day they took out their loans, was the last thing on their minds.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: "The conversation was just so much less relevant at that time," says Charlotte.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: Each borrowed about £37,500 to cover three years of tuition and living costs.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: They may have started out in the same position, but over that time their career trajectories, life choices and earnings have shaped how much they've repaid, how much interest they've racked up, and how much they owe - with very different outcomes.

sentences.text: The anger about Plan 2 grew after the government announced updated terms in November.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: But it has also been brewing because the interest rate is higher than most other student loan plans, and many have seen their debts rise despite making monthly repayments.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: "Since April this year, I've paid off in the region of £450 and I've accrued over £500 in interest," says Charlotte, a physiotherapist in Bristol.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: She did a master's degree after uni and worked in the NHS before moving to the private sector.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: She earns about £50,000, but her loan is still going up.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: "It makes me angry... it's just disheartening." All three friends earn above the national average of £39,039.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: But research from the Institute for Fiscal Studies , external in February suggests Plan 2 graduates need to earn about £63,000 or more for a loan balance of £50,000 to start going down.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: "I just had no concept that the debt was going to go up," says Libby, who remembers being in tears when her first student loan letter came through after graduating.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: Now a project manager in a housing association and living in Worcester, she earns £72,000 and says her student loan balance has hovered at about £47,000 for a number of years.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: But she is currently on maternity leave and knows the interest will continue to accrue while her earnings - and therefore monthly repayments - drop.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: "It feels like I will never pay it off, so it's something that I'm kind of just sucking up until the loan is written off," she says.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: Her partner did the same course, starting a year before her and before tuition fees near tripled with the introduction of Plan 2 loans.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: She says it is "so frustrating" that she has to pay out thousands of pounds a year more on her student debt.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: Current and former students have different student loan plans depending on where they live in the UK and when they went to university.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: Plan 2 loans were given out in England for a little more than a decade from 2012 and are still issued in Wales.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: The debt is written off after 30 years.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: Lizzy, who studied economics and now works in financial services and lives in Bristol, is the highest paid of the friends, who bonded over rowing at university.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: She earns £85,000 a year and decided last year to clear her student debt by borrowing money from her family instead.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: She had estimated that, based on her current earnings trajectory, she would repay her loan in 11 years.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: By paying off her debt in full early she has accrued less interest and hopes to repay her family in four years - saving about £20,000.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: Finance journalist Holly Mead told the BBC it could make sense for those who are confident they will clear the debt and can make "a really significant overpayment" of tens of thousands of pounds, like Lizzy.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: But smaller voluntary repayments could mean "you're just voluntarily paying more interest that you don't need to pay", she added.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: Lizzy, Charlotte and Libby say they are grateful they met at university and would go back if they had their time again The three friends pictured on Charlotte's wedding day Lizzy says she knows there are many "scenarios in which it doesn't pay off" for people to repay it early.

sentences.text: "I made a gamble on my future self to actually repay it," she says.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: "I'm in a very privileged position to be able to do that...
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: Buying your way out of the system or not being in at all is in itself a luxury.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: It buys you freedom." She and Libby finished their A-levels in 2011 but took a year out before going to university - Libby on a gap year, and Lizzy to resit economics after missing the grade she'd hoped for by a single mark.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: Lizzy says she knew the delay would mean her fees would be higher, but "it was never explained" that the repayment terms would "look and feel very different".
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: "I think that's something that took me probably the best part of 10 years to understand," she adds, noting that her twin sister did start university in 2011 and had less debt as a result.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: "Whether you went to uni in 2012 or 2011 actually financially has a huge impact, and it shouldn't," she says.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: An inquiry by MPs then concluded that this amounted to "mis-selling" because it was inaccurate for higher earners.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: Last month, the government said university applicants in England would be given clearer information about student loans before they take them out.

sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: All three friends follow the Rethink Repayment campaign on social media.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: It was set up by Oliver Gardner, who says the first Plan 2 borrowers are grappling with competing financial pressures such as getting on the property ladder and starting families.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: "Maybe in your 20s, you can get away without saving as much, potentially.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: But now people are like, 'we need the savings to do these big things that we want to do with our lives'," he says.
sentences.article_title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up

sentences.text: The campaign wants a lower Plan 2 interest rate, a lower repayment rate and for the government to reverse that decision to freeze the threshold at £29,385 in England for three years from 2027 - which, while it is not the first freeze, sparked this year's debate.

sentences.text: Gardner said the government was "engaging much more openly and honestly" but "the onus is very much on them in the upcoming October budget to take this by the reins" because graduates would not accept "minor tinkering around the edges".

sentences.text: The largest teaching union had objected to the prospect of partly funding a 3.5% pay increase this year out of existing school budgets Schools in England are to get around £500 million in extra funding towards the teachers' pay award this school year, reducing the risk of a strike ballot by the largest education union.

sentences.text: The channel went live on YouTube on Thursday (BBC News presenter Maryam Moshiri pictured) The BBC News channel has been made available to stream live on YouTube for viewers in the UK and USA.

sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: Danny Dyer led calls for nationalisation of the water industry on the River Thames on a float with a large poo sculpture on it Actor Danny Dyer has delivered a petition to Downing Street calling for water companies to be nationalised after floating a giant poo sculpture down the River Thames on a boat.
sentences.article_title: Danny Dyer in floating poo water protest on Thames

sentences.text: Dyer and Sittingbourne and Sheppey MP Kevin McKenna sailed along the Thames with the sculpture as part of a protest calling for the water industry to be brought into public ownership.
sentences.article_title: Danny Dyer in floating poo water protest on Thames

sentences.article_title: Danny Dyer in floating poo water protest on Thames

sentences.text: Amid drumming and dancing, Boateng Bismark James leads 13 worshippers, nine men and four women, in prayer for drivers and passengers travelling to destinations across Ghana.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Ghana is a predominantly Christian country where preaching on public transport is widespread.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: On long-distance buses, pastors can often be seen - and heard - preaching the gospel.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Sometimes they stand in the stairwell next to the driver, at others they walk up and down the aisle reading from the Bible and calling on sinners to repent at the tops of their voices.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: They do not stop even if the trip lasts for several hours.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: The faithful sometimes offer money to the preachers to support their endeavours.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: But a new law means this familiar practice could be coming to an end.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Anyone found preaching in public service vehicles faces up to eight months in prison, a fine of up to $52 (£39) or both.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: The new regulation, passed by parliament in May, and which has started to be enforced in recent weeks, targets preaching and hawking on vehicles while they are in motion, classifying both as a nuisance and citing the safety and comfort of passengers.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Boateng, a 61-year-old pastor at Gospel Light church, has been preaching on commercial vehicles leaving Neoplan station since 2023.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: "I preach on commercial vehicles because not everyone is able to go to church on Sunday.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: There are a lot of passengers who need our message of salvation to repent from their sins.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: We even heal the sick on some buses," he told the BBC in Twi, a local language.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Wearing a clerical collared shirt, Boateng moves through rows of buses loading passengers before boarding one bound for Kumasi, Ghana's second-largest city.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: We speak to him before the bus departs to avoid breaking the law.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Some travellers listen closely as he delivers his message.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Others try to ignore him, browsing their phones, making calls or chatting among themselves.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: "Some passengers are very happy with my message.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Some even say they have never heard the message in church, but through my preaching they now know it is in the Bible," he says.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Boateng Bismark James and his group start preaching at the bus station before boarding the vehicles The new rules have divided opinion.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Critics say preaching on moving vehicles is a nuisance and a safety risk, as it could distract the driver, while supporters argue that evangelism is a Christian duty and should be protected under the freedom of religious worship.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: One woman in her early 30s, who wishes to be identified as Chery Lokko, says she prefers to travel in peace. ''I don't like it because they are a nuisance.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Some of them spit saliva on you unconsciously, especially if you are seated not far from them, and they are a nuisance in terms of noise and saliva.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: I like my peace whenever I'm on public transport.'' In one video widely shared on social media recently, a passenger on a minibus is seen angrily confronting a pastor attempting to board.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: "Get down, I say get down," he shouts.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: But in this devout country, ranked among the most religious in the world , external , others say evangelism on public transport is an important way of reaching people who may not attend church.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Bernice Nartey, a passenger travelling to Kumasi, says pastors should be allowed to preach, but only with passengers' consent.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: "The preaching sometimes helps people to repent.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: For instance, if someone is going through a stressful situation, the message of the pastor can give the person renewed hope," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Boateng says he was shaken by the regulation and wants religious preachers to be given an exemption.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: "We are very worried, because most pastors here depend on preaching to take care of their families through the monetary gifts offered by passengers," he says.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: "The government should allow us to preach on the buses and alight when it is exiting Accra," he adds.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: For Boateng, preaching is not only a religious calling but also an important source of income.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: "I have been able to take care of my children's education.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Preaching on commercial buses was first prohibited in Ghana in 2012, with offenders facing up to 30 days in prison.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: But enforcement was weak and so the practice remained common, particularly on buses.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: The new law beefs up the penalties for those that flout the ban.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Preachers using megaphones can also often be seen and heard at Ghana's lorry parks and markets but they are not affected by the ban.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: The Christian Council of Ghana did not respond to the BBC's request for a comment but Rev Enoch Paul Hayes, a senior pastor at one of the biggest churches in Ghana, the International Central Gospel Church, tells the BBC he does not think the new rules infringe on religious freedom.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: He urges his fellow pastors not to break the law, saying they should find other ways of spreading their message.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: "There is social media as an alternative outlet, where the same message can reach thousands of people," he says.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer
